body: The NASCAR Hall of Famer, Daytona 500 winner and 34-time Cup Series victor stars in a cinematic campaign following a year of career highs and personal heartbreak.

A 34-time NASCAR Cup Series winner, 2004 Cup Series champion and 2017 Daytona 500 victor, Busch built his reputation as one of racing's fiercest competitors. The campaign traces his journey from a young boy with racing dreams to the pinnacle of American motorsports.

Originally developed in April 2026, production was temporarily paused following his family's loss, with the storyline reworked to deliver a more personal and heartfelt message. Busch personally selected the young actors portraying himself and his family.

"To me it's a perfect story of how you have to work hard. It's not going to be easy. You're going to have failures and you're going to get kicked around a little bit," said Busch. "The family, the losses, the work toward success, the wins, the championships, and then now the future of protecting all the nice stuff that you got."

Filmed at Arizona's Radford Racing School, where Busch trained as a rookie, the production features his personal 2020 Corvette C8, wrapped in Coverland branding and outfitted with custom-designed seat covers. Directed by Nicholas Markart, the film features high-speed driving sequences captured using Hollywood racing-film techniques, including a robotically controlled camera crane mounted to a moving vehicle. Matt Godoy wrote and produced the campaign alongside producer Jieying Wu and cinematographer Aleksei Doktorevitch. Early screenings among NASCAR influencers have drawn enthusiastic reactions to the nostalgic childhood scenes and Busch's return behind the wheel.

About Kurt Busch:Kurt Busch is a NASCAR Hall of Famer, 2004 NASCAR Cup Series champion and 2017 Daytona 500 winner. With 34 Cup Series victories and more than 700 starts across a career spanning two decades, Busch established himself among NASCAR's elite. Known for his versatility, competitive intensity and success across multiple generations of racing, he remains one of motorsports' most celebrated figures.

body: Presented by Monster Energy and built around Kotsenburg's vision for the sport, the new event will bring 24 of the world's best snowboarders to Jackson Hole's infamous Dick's Ditch during a two-week weather window from February 20 to March 6, 2027. In front of live spectators and streamed to fans worldwide, invited riders will battle on enhanced jumps and natural mountain features, proving their skills on Jackson Hole's world-famous deep snow.

"Jackson Hole is one of the most iconic destinations in snowboarding, and there's no better place to bring together some of the world's best riders for the Deep Snow Classic," said Cody Dresser, Global Vice President of Action Sports at Monster Energy. "This event is all about celebrating backcountry snowboarding, pushing the progression of the sport and giving these athletes a platform to showcase what makes riding deep snow so special."

"Few runs mean as much to snowboarding as Dick's Ditch," said Ned Wonson, Vice President of Marketing at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort. "Locals and legends have been progressing the sport there for decades, and we're thrilled to bring a backcountry-style session event to the ditch where fans can watch the best riders in the world compete up close."

The Deep Snow Classic will feature 24 invited pro riders, including 16 men and eight women, competing in a powder-focused freestyle contest at Dick's Ditch. The iconic natural halfpipe is well-known for its steep walls, narrow banked turns, rolling terrain, and natural hits and hips. The men's competition will feature three runs per rider, with the women's competition alternating between men's runs throughout the event.To make the most of fresh snowfall, the course build will begin with three to four days of ditch closure timed around a strong storm window, including one to two days of hand shaping to prepare the jumps and features.

Competition will then unfold over a single action-packed day. Riders will compete for awards in multiple categories, with one overall winner crowned for Best Overall Impression. Additional honors include top-three finishes for men and women, Best Trick awards, and the Bobby Martinez Award for Best Style, with the recipient taking home a Channel Islands Bobby Quad surfboard. A Polaris snowmobile will also be awarded as part of the competition. The invite-only contest will be followed by a Locals Session, giving Jackson Hole's own riders a chance to take on the course after the pros and earn the Local Legend award.

By popular demand, the inaugural Deep Snow Classic will give fans a rare opportunity to watch world-class backcountry-style snowboarding live and on-site. JHMR will offer spectator viewing areas at the venue, complemented by a lineup of events throughout the competition. Ticketed events include an opening party and bib draw, along with the official awards ceremony and after-party, while free events open to the public include an athlete meet-and-greet and poster signing, as well as live venue viewing.

body: In the latest edition of its CIO Compass, Sopra Steria Next broadens the debate on AI sovereignty: it is not only about where data and models reside, but also about who controls the decisions they produce.

It is not just a matter of knowing where data is hosted and where models run. It also covers the ability to demonstrate, at any moment, who controls, explains and arbitrates automated decisions. Vendor dependency has shifted from infrastructure to cognition, and that dependency is harder to reverse. With this publication, Sopra Steria Next calls on CIOs to make explicit a five-layer 'sovereignty stack', spanning data, models, platforms, APIs and decisions, with one question per layer: who operates it? Who can replace it? Who is accountable?

'The new question we now have to ask concerns decisions that AI has already taken without anyone being accountable for them,' says Valérie Thiblet, Partner Data & AI, Sopra Steria Next. 'A system that cannot be stopped in real time is not governed: it is merely observed. And what cannot be governed cannot be industrialised.'

The document identifies several breaking points for IT departments: the rise of Shadow AI, which erodes traceability and cost control before leaders are even aware of it; model governance, still treated as an optional layer; and the AI Act, where the main risk will not be deliberate non-compliance but accidental non-compliance through lack of preparation.

As reflected in the public Judgment, the litigation arose from Brent Evan Smith's exclusion from Phoenix Gems do Brasil Ltda. in June 2007, approximately three years after execution of the June 5, 2004 Serra Pelada agreements referenced in Phoenix Gems' July 1, 2026 news release. The Judgment further records that the Plaintiff sought, among other relief, the annulment of legal transactions entered into after the June 2007 exclusion, notably those involving Colossus Mineração Ltda.

Following consideration of the evidence and applicable Brazilian law, the Court declared the June 2007 contractual amendment excluding Brent Evan Smith from Phoenix Gems do Brasil Ltda. null and void, holding that restoration of the status quo ante required his reintegration as a shareholder with all corresponding rights and obligations, thereby restoring the legal framework that existed prior to the June 2007 exclusion. The Court further declared subsequent legal transactions dependent upon the validity of that exclusion to be null, while preserving the rights of good-faith third parties, awarded damages for moral harm, and dismissed counterclaims.

The Judgment became final (transitado em julgado) on June 4, 2026. According to the official public docket, on July 6, 2026, the Court issued a certificate and remitted the case file to the 1ª Contadoria de Custas for further proceedings in the judgment enforcement phase (cumprimento de sentença), where the post-judgment proceedings continue in accordance with Brazilian judicial procedure.

The complete Judgment and procedural history remain publicly available through the Tribunal de Justiça de Pernambuco's Public Consultation Portal. We encourage investors, regulators, industry participants, and all interested stakeholders to review the public judicial record in its entirety.

title: Jury Awards $17 Million to Woman Whose Bladder Was Mistakenly Removed During Routine Surgery
excerpt: A Kennebec County jury awarded $17 million on July 23, 2026, to Emily Mitchell, whose bladder was mistakenly removed during what was intended...

expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Jury represents a significant milestone in verifiable regulation infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Two of Maine's leading medical malpractice attorneys secure verdict in catastrophic surgical error case.

The case arose from a March 1, 2023, laparoscopic procedure performed to remove a benign ovarian cyst after imaging showed it had increased significantly in size. According to evidence presented at trial, what began as a routine gynecologic surgery resulted in one of the most devastating surgical errors imaginable.

Following the procedure, Emily's condition worsened, and she was transferred to Eastern Maine Medical Center in Bangor for emergency surgery. There, surgeons discovered that her bladder had been mistakenly removed during the original operation. Pathology confirmed that the tissue removed during the procedure consisted of full-thickness bladder tissue, and surgeons determined there was insufficient healthy bladder tissue remaining to reconstruct or repair the organ.

For more than eight months, Emily relied on bilateral nephrostomy tubes to drain urine directly from her kidneys while enduring recurrent urinary tract infections, kidney infections, multiple medical procedures, and ongoing complications. She was eventually referred to Massachusetts, where surgeons performed a complex reconstructive surgery using a portion of her small intestine to create a neobladder.

Today, Emily continues to live with the permanent effects of those injuries. She requires self-catheterization multiple times each day, ongoing medical treatment, and continued care from specialists related to the loss of her bladder.

After hearing the evidence, the jury found Northern Light Inland Hospital and Northern Light Health liable and awarded $17 million in damages for past and future medical expenses, past and future pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, emotional distress, and permanent impairment.

The data suggest AI is not yet driving widespread staffing reductions. According to IDC, 57.9% of respondents said AI has had no impact on their hiring, and more reported increasing hiring (24.2%) than decreasing it (9.2%).

"Many have predicted that AI will end the billable hour on the theory that faster work will lead clients to demand task-based billing," said Horrigan. "The research indicates that has not happened broadly, at least not yet."

África se ve dificultada por realidades normativas muy diferentes en todo el continente, que van desde mercados totalmente prohibidos hasta aquellos con marcos normativos introducidos recientemente. Se complica aún más por la presencia y persistencia del sector no regulado, que busca explotar cualquier mercado independientemente de sus condiciones normativas.

El desafío de África: De lo no regulado a lo regulado

Este informe reconoce la magnitud del desafío al que se enfrenta África. En el año 2025, los operadores de juego en línea no regulados robaron 17.800 millones de dólares en ingresos brutos del juego en línea, lo que costó a los gobiernos africanos aproximadamente 3.550 millones de dólares en impuestos perdidos. El número de operadores no regulados que operan en África aumentó de 3.644 en 2024 a 4.129 en 2025.

GCI presenta estas pérdidas como los posibles beneficios futuros de la optimización del mercado. A medida que la cuota de mercado se traslade al sector regulado, habrá más consumidores protegidos, se generarán más empleos e inversiones locales y se dispondrá de más financiación pública para el crecimiento y desarrollo de las comunidades.

body: This partnership introduces the first Web3 digital currency settlement protocol to ONERWAY that provides merchants with new choices for digital currency settlement while retaining its fiat settlement advantages—backed by its multiple payment licenses, including UK EMI, European PI, Hong Kong MSO, US MSB, and Singapore MPI, as well as principal membership qualifications with major credit cards such as Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay International, and Discover, and PCI DSS Level 1 security certification. For HSP, ONERWAY is the first traditional Web2 payment partner. Through strategic integration with a licensed payment institution, HSP extends its on-chain settlement capabilities to ONERWAY's existing network of over 2,000 merchants spanning multiple vertical sectors including cross-border e-commerce, gaming and entertainment, digital content subscriptions, and SaaS, achieving a shift from the protocol layer to real-world commercial scenarios.

Problems in cross-border payments have persisted for a long time such as long settlement cycles, exchange losses, and complex multi-currency accounting. For cross-border e-commerce and digital service enterprises, these issues directly impact operational efficiency and cash flow turnover.

Stablecoins offer a potential path to a solution—on-chain settlement is near-real-time while cross-border flows require few to no intermediaries, and exchange rate risks can be controlled through lock-up mechanisms. However, the issue for most merchants is how to convert funds into local fiat currency that can be used to pay suppliers, employee salaries, or meet tax compliance requirements after receiving stablecoins. There is a strong need to improve the utilization of on-chain assets and capital efficiency.

This partnership aims to provide a blockchain bridge. HSP is driven by two core modules: the Master Account, which handles intelligent aggregation and distribution of merchants' on-chain funds, and the Settlement Protocol, which provides the foundation for transaction authorization verification standards to ensure that every transaction is auditable. HashKey Group's licensed entities provide custody and OTC services, utilizing the HSP protocol as the technical pathway to connect with ONERWAY's licensed fiat channels. After completing on-chain stablecoin settlement, ONERWAY merchants can leverage its own licensed fiat channels and the technical circulation path with HSP to convert the funds into local fiat currency, which can be used to pay suppliers or distribute employee salaries, while also facilitating merchants in meeting their own tax reporting requirements.
Compliance as pillar to Accelerate the Adoption of Stablecoin Payments

Licensed entities under HashKey Group hold relevant digital asset service licenses in Hong Kong and are among the few institutions in Asia capable of providing digital asset services within a complete regulatory framework. The HSP settlement protocol natively integrates on-chain AML mechanisms to ensure transactions are secure and auditable. Meanwhile, ONERWAY's multi-jurisdictional licensing ensures the compliant operation of fiat channels across major markets. Both companies support the large-scale adoption of stablecoin payments with compliant infrastructure.

Ray Soudah, président et fondateur de Millenium Associates AG, a déclaré : « Nous avons été approchés par de nombreuses plateformes cette année. Nous apprécions Ittikar parce que les personnes qui la dirigent ont passé vingt-cinq ans dans les mêmes locaux que nous, parce qu'elle est conçue pour l'investisseur plutôt que pour le vendeur, et parce qu'elle a déjà conclu plusieurs transactions concrètes. L'analyse devient une marchandise, alors que le réseau et le jugement ne le sont pas, et l'innovation d'Ittikar réunit les deux. Nos clients et notre réseau auront désormais la possibilité d'accéder directement à des familles et des entrepreneurs capables d'investir avec plus de sagesse et de confiance ».

Hussam Otaibi, fondateur d'Ittikar et de Mondevo Group, a déclaré : « Je connais Ray Soudah depuis plus de quinze ans en tant que vétéran de notre secteur, et son avis sur les transactions est selon moi le meilleur pour accompagner nos agents de plateforme. Ce qui fait la différence, ce sont les personnes qui en font leur métier depuis vingt-cinq ans et qui utilisent désormais cette technologie au quotidien. Crest and LBAF were developed around two different objectives. Crest is USD-denominated and seeks to generate returns above US Treasury bill yields, while LBAF is designed for investors who measure returns in Bitcoin units and targets net annualised returns of 8–12 percent in Bitcoin terms.

To bring the funds onchain, CMCC Global turned to two partners operating at scale. "By partnering with Tether and Bitfinex Securities we are selecting issuance technology proven at the scale of the world's largest stablecoin, USDt, together with a regulated venue purpose-built for tokenised securities." Yesterday, the U.S. House Administration Committee hearing entitled "Preventing Fraudulent Donations: Transparency, Verification, and Accountability" largely focused on Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and his failure to address campaign finance violations at WinRed, the fundraising platform bankrolling his own Senate campaign. body: Bain's Future of Banking report argues that AI is more than a tool for productivity gains. It can also extend market leadership positions by helping banks build value propositions that win share faster. That is because rapidly changing AI advances are shifting which banking businesses stay attractive, which competitive differentiators endure, and which customer relationships are worth defending.

The stakes are high for market leaders defending their positions and the challengers looking to take customer share. Return on equity (ROE) at the world's largest banks has not recovered since the global financial crisis. And Bain's analysis shows market leadership matters: among the top 30 banks by 2025 year-end assets, banks with number 1 or close number 2 positions in their business lines earn a 15% ROE, versus 9% for those with weaker positions.

Using AI to reinforce or build leadership positions is central to restoring returns, more so than efficiency gains alone. Banks have long relied on inertia to slow customers from comparing offers or switching providers. But AI is poised to lower barriers to entry, making switching frictionless. Banks will need to reassess where to defend their leadership, says Bain.
The brief identifies four "hard truths" for an AI-led future:

Bain recommends banks consider three strategic responses: 1) build and attack where AI makes new propositions possible; 2) defend and deepen where profit pools stay structurally attractive; and 3) rethink participation where economics depend on friction AI could remove.

"The AI-enabled customer cuts both ways for banks, particularly as agents remove friction from switching," said Peter Stumbles, partner and global head of Bain's Financial Services practice. "The opportunity to further personalize offerings and enable customers is real, but so is the threat of deposit churn and customer defection. A far larger contestable market than before means yesterday's incumbent strategy won't be defensible today. Leadership in chosen markets, with a winning proposition with chosen customer segments, will matter more than ever."

On February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court of the United States held that the tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), 50 U.S.C. § 1701 et seq., were unlawful, and it invalidated the tariff orders issued under that statute.

Beginning in early 2025, the federal government imposed sweeping tariffs on imported goods under the purported authority of the IEEPA, sharply increasing the cost of importing consumer products into the United States. body: The AI platform from former Google and Verily leaders processes raw data from new and past experiments, so researchers can test findings against existing evidence and train AI models on it

AI models of biology are limited by the experimental data they learn from, and funders are now paying to produce more. On Oct. 7, Biohub, Google DeepMind, Meta, Isomorphic Labs, and U.S. agencies announced a $1.8 billion effort to generate and standardize biological data for AI. Tesorai complements these efforts by starting with data that already exists, reprocessing and harmonizing thousands of publicly available datasets to recover information that was previously missed and make it available to scientists and AI developers.

Raw data from millions of experiments sits scattered across public repositories, institutional archives, and company databases, processed with different methods and often poorly annotated. Rather than simply indexing papers or aggregating existing analyses, Tesorai's AI goes back to that raw data, which holds far more information than older analysis methods could accurately and quickly extract, and harmonizes the results across studies so researchers can search and compare them.

The result is a new way for researchers to interact with scientific knowledge: asking questions not just about what has been published, but about what the experiments themselves reveal. Tesorai Search processes that data in the cloud, whether it comes from a lab's newest experiment or a study published years ago, and its patented model has processed thousands of files and terabytes of data in just a few hours, which previously required months to complete. Tesorai Chat runs downstream analyses using conversational prompts, a task that usually requires bioinformaticians, and Tesorai Trove empowers researchers to validate and cross-analyze their results against tens of thousands of past studies.

"Life science R&D is accelerating and becoming increasingly autonomous, which makes it more important to extract as much insight as possible from every experiment," said Charlie Kim, co-founder and chief scientific officer of Tesorai. "Tesorai does this for a lab's new data and for thousands of published studies. The gains compound as each experiment builds on the last, and ultimately, this helps the industry develop better medicines and products, faster."

The potential of this approach is already becoming tangible. To test the Alzheimer's panel, published in JAMA Neurology on Aug. 10, Tesorai's team reprocessed raw files from five public brain studies and recovered p-tau217, one of the panel's seven proteins and a leading Alzheimer's marker, which none of the original studies had previously reported. It posted the analysis as a preprint three weeks later.

Der neue Bericht „Online-Glücksspiel 2024–2025: EU 27 Europe", der von Gaming Compliance International (GCI) für die Campaign for Fairer Gambling (CFG) erstellt wurde, kommt zu dem Ergebnis, dass der unregulierte Online-GGR von 52,6 Milliarden Euro 2023 auf 91,6 Milliarden Euro im Jahr 2025 gestiegen ist – ein Anstieg von 74 % innerhalb von zwei Jahren.

2025 erzielten unregulierte Online-Glücksspielanbieter mit Verbrauchern aus der EU-27 einen geschätzten Bruttospielertrag (GGR) von 91,6 Milliarden Euro – das entspricht 72 % des europäischen Online-Glücksspielmarktes mit einem Gesamtvolumen von 128,0 Milliarden Euro. How PAPY works. Lenders deposit AUSD into the PAPY vault on the Morpho protocol. Those deposits are then lent to borrowers who post white-listed RWA collateral and pay an algorithmically derived, variable interest rate. For the PAPY vault, Bitwise's curation involves predetermining the vault's parameters and precalibrating its models—including acceptable collateral, loan-to-value ratios, and interest-rate configuration—without taking custody of or exercising discretionary management over user assets.

AUSD, the deposit asset. Deposits are made in AUSD, Agora's stablecoin, which is fully collateralized by U.S. Treasury bills, overnight and reverse repo, and other liquid assets. AUSD's reserves are managed by VanEck and custodied at State Street.
Note: All descriptions and figures above are as stated by provider.

Why RWAs? Most onchain yield today comes from two crowded models: commoditized bitcoin-backed lending or crypto-native yield farming. PAPY offers a more durable approach. Loans secured by RWAs tap deeper traditional-finance credit markets, so the interest borrowers pay isn't tied to crypto cycles or onchain liquidity.

"We believe a diverse basket of collateral gives users a better risk-adjusted lending experience, but that only works with a specialist curator," said Jonathan Man, Portfolio Manager at Bitwise. "Our team brings 20-plus years of experience across structured credit, private credit, and the technology behind DeFi, and that's what informs our approach to bringing real-world asset collateral onchain with the Bitwise Premium RWA Vault."

body: Fraud and scams cross sectors and borders, but the organizations working to prevent them often use different ways to classify and describe threats. These differences can make fraud patterns identified in one organization or region difficult to interpret and address in another, limiting the reach of detecting fraud. OFTA will develop a technical interoperability layer connecting existing fraud and scam taxonomies and typologies to help organizations understand and apply fraud data developed across different regions without replacing their own frameworks, standards or systems.

Working with established intelligence and signal-sharing partners, OFTA will identify emerging fraud patterns, recommend new or updated taxonomies and typologies, and incorporate those developments into its interoperability framework. It will also develop practical defense playbooks that organizations can apply within their own regulatory environments, turning shared expertise into coordinated action that strengthens financial systems and protects the people who rely on them.

"Aligning how industries classify and understand financial crime is essential to a coordinated response," said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. "OFTA brings together the frameworks, resources and expertise to make that possible. Neutral governance gives organizations a trusted place to turn what they learn individually into practical defenses they can build and improve together."

Tazama, a Linux Foundation Charities project, brings an open source technology platform to this ecosystem, helping financial institutions and payment ecosystems monitor transactions and detect potential fraud and money laundering. OFTA's work will complement technologies such as Tazama by connecting fraud prevention frameworks and developing practical guidance that organizations can apply through their own systems.

OFTA received a grant from the Gates Foundation to support its launch. Initial members include Cifas, The Knoble, Mobile Ecosystem Forum (MEF), and Stop Scams Alliance. Feedzai and The Global Anti-Scam Alliance also endorsed the Foundation.

OFTA invites financial institutions, payment networks, telecommunications providers, digital platforms, fraud prevention organizations and public-sector bodies to contribute their expertise to its interoperability framework and practical defense playbooks. To learn more, visit https://ofta.io.

body: Among the study's findings are several notable trends impacting the industry today. Most significantly, RV shopping cycles have lengthened, with 45% of shoppers saying they take four months or longer (an increase of 12 percentage points since 2023) to conclude their buying experience. Marine shopping journeys are similarly extended, with 40% taking four months or more, while powersports buyers are also demonstrating longer consideration periods, with 51% spending more than one month shopping before making a purchase. The learnings point to brands and dealers needing to build long-term lead nurture strategies to engage consumers over extended decision-making periods.

Consumers place the highest level of trust in manufacturer websites, with 88% to 94% of respondents across segments saying they trust information provided directly by OEMs. Dealer information also remains highly trusted, but shoppers increasingly supplement both sources with third-party resources and owner communities to validate pricing, availability, quality, and ownership experiences. At the same time, AI is emerging as a meaningful research tool in the buying journey, creating an opportunity for brands to provide trusted, always-available product expertise. When asked how they would use an AI agent, 61% of respondents said they want answers to specific product questions, while 65% want guidance on insurance, financing, and cost of ownership, highlighting a growing demand for AI-powered product specialists that help consumers make informed decisions earlier in the shopping process.

The research also highlights a significant increase in demand for digital shopping experiences. Consumers increasingly prefer completing research, inventory searches, financing research, trade evaluations, and quoting requests online before ever stepping into a dealership. More than half of respondents in every segment also said they prefer to explore financing online, while a desire for online credit approval reached 54% in RV and 62% in both powersports and marine. Yet despite growing digital expectations, the dealership remains the preferred destination for finalizing purchases and taking delivery, reinforcing the importance of a connected online-to-offline buying journey.

Affordability emerged as one of the most important themes of the study. Pricing was the leading reason prospects did not purchase in the previous 12 months, cited by 26% of RV respondents, 27% of powersports respondents, and 32% of marine respondents. Looking ahead, approximately 84% of consumers said product price increases would affect their future purchase decisions, up from approximately 74% in the 2023 study.

"The outdoor recreation marketplace continues to evolve, but one thing remains constant: consumers expect a simpler, more informed buying experience," said Bernie Brenner, CEO of Rollick. "The 2026 Future of Buying Study serves as a strategic roadmap for OEMs, dealers, and industry leaders seeking to understand the next generation of outdoor recreation buyers." Biała księga koncentruje się na kluczowych zdolnościach, takich jak tworzenie sieci, wsparcie częstotliwości, wsparcie napięciowe, wzmacnianie sztywności systemu oraz wsparcie w stanach zakłóceniowych. Uwzględniając m.in. szybkość reakcji, poziom wsparcia i granice pracy, przenosi ocenę zdolności w zakresie tworzenia sieci z opisu funkcji na mierzalną weryfikację parametrów. The service responds to a marked shift in adjudication. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services data shows the EB-1A approval rate fell to approximately 53% in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, down from roughly 67% for the full year. Immigration attorneys report a parallel rise in RFEs and closer examination of evidence at the final merits stage, with officers placing greater weight on whether an applicant's recognition is selective, independently validated, and sustained.

Global Talent PR secures coverage exclusively through earned media, working directly with editors and reporters at established trade and industry outlets. The firm does not pay for placements. Because coverage is organic, it reflects genuine editorial interest rather than payment. Paid or sponsored coverage has never been accepted by USCIS, and applicants who have drawn an RFE face closer examination of the provenance of their evidence, making the distinction between earned and paid coverage more consequential at this stage than at any other point in the process.

"An RFE means an officer is looking closely, and the evidence in a response has to hold up to that scrutiny," said Kristen Hoff, co-founder of Global Talent PR. "Earned coverage carries weight precisely because it cannot be bought. We identify where an applicant's expertise genuinely meets editorial interest and work on an accelerated timeline so the placements are in hand when the response is due."

"When a petition receives an RFE, the response should contain independent, objective, and verifiable evidence of the applicant's recognition and impact within the field. Particularly compelling are materials that objectively demonstrate the applicant's influence outside of their own institution, such as industry publications, conference presentations, invitations to speak, or other third-party materials that specifically identify the applicant by name and discuss their contributions. In our experience, the ability to document multiple independent sources referencing the applicant by name carries significant weight in demonstrating sustained acclaim," said Radu C. Vasilescu of The Vasilescu Law Firm.

The Final Merits service follows the same standards as the firm's standard engagements, with placements aligned to each applicant's petition and coordinated with their immigration counsel before publication.

"Deal flow was never the constraint in this market. Discipline was. This transaction has all four, and we believe it represents the most attractive risk-adjusted return we have underwritten to date. I am genuinely excited about the growth potential it unlocks for Forum, and we are intensely focused on the execution that will generate that growth, one site at a time."

The transaction supports Forum's strategy of acquiring, structuring, financing and operating cash-generating assets with attractive risk-adjusted returns in large, complex markets with durable demand drivers. Forum has previously identified AI infrastructure as one of its four key vertical markets, alongside commercial aerospace, manufactured housing finance and auto credit. Forum's pipeline of AI infrastructure deals has been a key 2026 priority, and the Joint Venture represents a major step forward in both expanding access to financing and tokenization opportunities and integrating strategic asset ownership with a highly differentiated, risk-controlled and modular approach. The Joint Venture is focused on inference, the workload that runs trained AI models in production, which in many use cases is required to sit close to the users it serves. Forum Edge AI's platform architecture addresses this demand for low-latency, edge compute by placing its sites inside metropolitan areas rather than in remote campuses. Simultaneously, this approach unlocks existing spare power, connectivity and physical sites rather than undertaking lengthy new greenfield builds.

"The next phase of AI infrastructure will require more than simply adding GPU capacity—it will require a distributed compute architecture that brings high-performance inference closer to where workloads and customers operate. Edge Node AI has been built around that vision," said Mallik Panda, founder and chief executive officer of Edge Node AI. "Forum brings significant capabilities in capital markets, financing, structuring, power and GPU supply that are highly complementary to our technical and operating capabilities. Together, we believe Forum Edge AI provides a strong platform to deploy infrastructure rapidly across powered data centers and distributed edge locations while maintaining disciplined, project-level economics. We are excited to work alongside Forum to build and scale this platform."

The Joint Venture will initiate and own the various projects which, discretely, deliver compute. These projects are organized in a hub-and-spoke manner, with the "spokes" as tower sites and the "hubs" as owned data centers from which equipment at the tower sites can also be serviced and maintained by Forum Edge AI personnel. To mitigate risk, each AI compute site will be held in a distinct project-level SPV, and each project will be capitalized, financed and closed independently of the others, with no cross-collateralization between projects. Where a project includes real property, the land and the compute equipment will be held in separate entities, ensuring that equipment financing does not encumber real estate and real estate financing does not encumber the equipment.

Forum is the sole manager and 51% owner of the Joint Venture and will consolidate its financial performance. All project revenue will flow to the Joint Venture, and operating expenses will be charged to the Joint Venture at actual cost with no markup. Forum will hold a right of first refusal on any data center or tower site originated by Edge Node AI, as well as on compute capacity across all projects. Edge Node AI will license its variable-load inference technology to the Joint Venture and will provide senior technical and operating capabilities and personnel to run the data centers and edge nodes on a day-to-day basis.

Forum and Edge Node AI will exchange 9.95% equity stakes in each respective company, subject to the achievement of certain power and financing milestones by the Joint Venture. Edge Node AI will receive approximately 1.46 million shares of Forum's common stock, representing approximately 9.95% of its shares outstanding after giving effect to the issuance, based on 13.2 million shares outstanding as of October 2, 2026. Both parties are subject to lock-up restrictions on the shares that may be issued. The cross-ownership is intended to align Forum's and Edge Node AI's interests in the long-term performance of the platform.

Iridium NTN Direct provides a reliable, truly global connection in remote grazing areas where cellular coverage is limited or absent, representing the kind of high-volume, low-power IoT deployment the service is designed for.

"Cattle grazes in some of the most remote land on Earth and losing a signal shouldn't mean losing sight of the herd. excerpt: APX Lending ("APX"), Canada's first regulated digital-asset credit infrastructure company, today announced the launch of its new 90/85...

expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from APX represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: 80% warning. 90% trigger. 85% reset. 0% liquidation fee.

For Bitcoin-backed borrowers, one of the greatest fears is losing the Bitcoin they specifically chose to borrow against instead of selling. That can happen through counterparty failure, a risk APX was built to mitigate through a regulated lending model, or through liquidation when Bitcoin prices fall. The 90/85 Standard is designed to address the second.

"Borrowers choose to borrow against Bitcoin precisely because they don't want to sell it," said Andrei Poliakov, Founder and CEO of APX Lending. "We believe in Bitcoin, and we want our borrowers to keep as much of it as possible. A momentary market move shouldn't unnecessarily liquidate a position someone may have spent years accumulating. Liquidation exists to protect the loan. It shouldn't sell more Bitcoin than necessary, and it shouldn't be a profit centre for lenders"

Under many crypto-backed lending models, reaching the liquidation threshold can result in most or all of a borrower's collateral being sold, either to repay the loan entirely or return it to its originating LTV.

Consider a borrower with $100,000 of collateral and a $90,000 loan. Under full liquidation with no fee, $90,000 of collateral would be sold, leaving $10,000 of collateral. With a 5% liquidation fee, $94,737 of collateral would be sold, leaving just $5,263 of collateral.

Under APX's 90/85 Standard, only $33,333 of collateral would be sold and applied against the loan, leaving the borrower with $66,667 of collateral and a $56,667 loan balance, resetting the loan to 85% LTV.

title: Before You Hand Down That Old Phone, Make Sure You're Not Giving Away Your Personal Information
excerpt: Mercury Insurance (NYSE/NYSE TX: MCY) is reminding consumers that an old smartphone, tablet, laptop or gaming console may contain more than a...
lede: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, making it an ideal time to examine an often-overlooked security risk: the personal information left behind on devices that change hands.

body: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, making it an ideal time to examine an often-overlooked security risk: the personal information left behind on devices that change hands.

"Most people think about protecting their information while they're using a device, but they don't always consider what happens to that information when they're finished with it," said Dustin Howard, Head of Information Security at Mercury Insurance. "An old phone or laptop can hold years of personal information, and simply deleting a few files or applications doesn't mean that information is gone. And always factory reset your device."
Five Steps to Take Before Passing Along Used Electronics

Before resetting a device, save important photographs, contacts, documents and other files to a secure cloud account or external storage device. Verify that the backup is complete and accessible before deleting anything. Consumers should also make sure they can access their accounts and authentication methods from another device.

Smartphones, tablets and computers can remain connected to email, cloud storage, banking applications, shopping accounts and subscription services. Sign out of accounts and remove the device from associated account-management settings when appropriate. Disable device-tracking and activation-lock features according to the manufacturer's instructions so the next user can properly set up the device.

Deleting individual files or uninstalling applications may leave information behind. Use the manufacturer's recommended procedure to erase personal data and restore the device to its original settings. Some older devices and storage systems may require additional steps to securely remove information. When a device cannot be reliably erased, recycling it through a reputable electronics program that offers secure data destruction may be the safer choice.

Sensitive data leaves through a file shared to a cloud drive, a form posted to a web app, or source code pasted into AI tools. Much of it has no fixed format, so rules looking for an account number or ID string let it pass. DLP that depends on data labels has a second gap: a file that is mislabeled or never labeled falls outside the policy, and it leaks.

In AI DLP, AI/ML classification and deep content inspection read what the data contains as it moves. File analysis and OCR read documents and the text inside images, and classification finds sensitive data whether it is labeled, mislabeled or not labeled at all. Where Microsoft Information Protection labels exist, AI DLP also reads and enforces them inline.

Policies set by user, group and department detect, flag or block source code, customer data, PII and intellectual property in real time, with a full audit trail. The same policies cover AI platforms and tools, so teams can keep sensitive data out of AI without banning the tools. They also apply when AI agents move the data, with control over which AI services, tools and APIs agents may use, and agent activity is retained.
AI DLP adds data-loss risk scoring and one-click GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS and SOX reports that give auditors evidence of what was found and stopped.

AI DLP runs on the iboss containerized architecture. Each customer's traffic is processed in dedicated containers with isolated SSL keys and dedicated IPs, and customer data is never co-mingled. It works alongside the iboss Secure Web Gateway, CASB, GenAI Protection and Zero Trust Network Access, with one console, one policy engine and one data lake.

body: New primary market route, built with Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network, allows approved institutions to mint and redeem Ondo Stocks using existing share inventory instead of cash, supporting tighter spreads and deeper secondary market liquidity
The addition allows institutions to convert existing share inventory directly into onchain liquidity, supporting tighter spreads and deeper liquidity for Ondo Stocks across secondary markets.

The integration automates the conversion process, removing the need for manual approval on each transaction and allowing institutions to move quickly between traditional share inventory and tokenized positions.

To mint, an approved institution transfers underlying shares from its Alpaca account to Ondo's Alpaca account via an internal book transfer; the corresponding Ondo Stocks tokens are then issued on the supported blockchain. Redemption reverses the process, returning the underlying shares to the institution's Alpaca account in exchange for the tokens.

Ondo Stocks connects tokenized stocks and ETFs to the liquidity of traditional markets, including Nasdaq and NYSE, through a just-in-time minting and redemption model. This integration extends that model by making it more capital-efficient for institutions to supply liquidity across secondary markets.

Under the cash-funded model, an institution holding underlying shares must source separate cash to mint tokens — a step that can introduce financing costs and a timing mismatch between its share inventory and tokenized positions. Direct access to Alpaca's ITN removes that step, making it easier for market makers to replenish token inventory, manage exposure, and respond to demand across trading venues. As a result, institutional capital becomes a more readily available source of tokenized stock liquidity in secondary markets — supporting tighter spreads and greater depth across the exchanges, wallets, and DeFi applications connected to the Ondo Stocks ecosystem.

"By bringing this facility online with Securitize, we're helping close the gap between traditional market hours and the always-on nature of blockchain markets. The facility launches with $50 million in initial liquidity, comprising $25 million in USDC and $25 million in BUIDL. As liquidity is utilized, an additional $50 million can be made available within an hour, bringing the facility's total capacity to $100 million. Founded in 2023 by Bobby Dillard and Tyler Buckler, BYPG is vertically integrated across acquisitions, asset management, development, and operations. Its principals previously led Cielo Property Group, where they executed more than $800 million in retail and office investments between 2010 and 2022. Their approach has been to identify sector shifts early, from post-crisis suburban retail to creative and technology office, and to execute directly as developers and operators. Since forming BYPG, the team has developed 250,000 square feet of bulk logistics space and repositioned 135,000 square feet of infill shallow-bay industrial.

The platform will target manufacturing facilities with in-place power infrastructure, serving manufacturers in aerospace and defense, electrification, energy, advanced materials and the digital infrastructure supply chain, with initial focus on Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Austin–San Antonio, Phoenix and the Carolinas' I-85 corridor. The strategy seeks to capitalize on the rapidly growing demand for manufacturing facilities with sufficient power, amid increasing constraints on the U.S. power grid.

Manufacturing now accounts for 20 percent of new industrial leasing in the Southeast and Central U.S., up from 13 percent before the pandemic, yet larger users face one- to two-year delays to secure sufficient power, according to PwC and the Urban Land Institute's Emerging Trends in Real Estate 2026. For those users, a building with power already in place is the fastest path to production. By acquiring and repositioning high-powered facilities, BYPG aims to capitalize on this supply-demand imbalance, turning existing grid capacity into ready-to-operate manufacturing space, and helping close the gap between where demand is growing and where power is available.

The first acquisition under the strategy, 2000 Clovis Barker Road in San Marcos, Texas, is a 75,276-square-foot, crane-served manufacturing facility on approximately 30 acres along the I-35 corridor between Austin and San Antonio. The property benefits from 2.5 megawatts of secured power capacity, and BYPG has executed a long-term lease with an established national industrial pipe fabrication company that will fully occupy the facility at closing.

Ermias Nessibu, Executive Director, Real Estate at GCM Grosvenor, said, "Our real estate strategy is built on partnering with specialized operators and helping them scale into institutional investment management platforms. Bobby, Tyler and the BYPG team have a proven track record of identifying emerging opportunities and executing in operationally complex sectors. Growing demand for high-power manufacturing facilities is colliding with limited suitable inventory, high development barriers and constrained access to power. We believe these structural supply-demand dynamics create a compelling investment opportunity, and we look forward to partnering with BYPG to build a leading institutional platform focused on this underserved segment of the industrial market "

FutureSports previously raised a seed investment round co-led by Marquee Ventures, spun out of the ownership group of the Chicago Cubs. Major financial industry leaders joined the round, including CME Ventures (the corporate venture capital division of CME Group), Robinhood Markets, Inc., WEDBUSH and DRW Special Investments (an investment arm of DRW). Other investors include Motivate VC, Phoenix Capital Ventures, and John and Linda Henry (Fenway Sports Group).

The company also announced the addition of industry experts to its board of directors, including Chairman Mark Wassersug, longtime Chief Operating & Information Officer of Intercontinental Exchange (ICE); Tim McCourt, Senior Managing Director, Global Head of Equity, FX, and Alternative Products at CME Group, and Erik Hammer, Managing Partner at Marquee Ventures.

The firm will soon unveil its first series of exclusive partnerships with major sports leagues, paving the way for institutional investors and companies in and around the sports industry to manage their risk in an unprecedented fashion and participate in regulated, tradable, broad-based index futures contracts based on team and athlete statistical performance. FutureSports creates rules-based financial indexes, known as FutureSports Performance Indexes (FSPI), that accurately represent the performance of teams and athletes in prominent sports leagues. By utilizing transparent, rules-based methodologies based on officially reported statistical outcomes, the company creates continuous values designed to underpin tradable financial products, such as listed derivatives, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and over-the-counter (OTC) swaps.

Potential market participants will include league broadcasting partners, team and athlete sponsors and endorsers, insurers, stadium owners and operators, private equity investors, lenders, and apparel manufacturers. Asset managers, pension funds and professional trading firms are expected to participate in the contracts and contribute to liquidity in this new uncorrelated asset class. Retail investors will also be able to participate in the first-of-their-kind trading vehicles, which the company expects to capture the interest of sophisticated traders looking for more traditional financial trading instruments

Leigh Taylforth, FutureSports Co-Founder, said: "The global sporting industry generates $650 billion a year, yet there has been no liquid, robust opportunity to hedge the extensive and varied industry risks that range from weather events, to injuries, to unanticipated behavior issues and more. That is about to change. We've been truly gratified to see the interest our business has generated within the sports and sports-adjacent industries and the quality of investors we have attracted already."

expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Edera represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: As enterprises increasingly deploy AI coding agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and other autonomous workloads into production, they face a fundamental security dilemma: agents need access to repositories, APIs and infrastructure to perform useful work, but giving them credentials and broad permissions creates significant risk if they are compromised or manipulated through prompt injection.

Edera's Bounded Authority addresses this problem by separating what an agent is allowed to do from the credentials required to do it. Rather than placing sensitive tokens inside an agent's execution environment, Edera enables platform and security teams to grant narrowly defined capabilities that are enforced outside the workload. This practical implementation of object capabilities is enforced by the hypervisor.

For example, an AI coding agent can be authorized to work within a single GitHub repository without possessing a GitHub token. The OCAP bounded authority also limits the scope of GitHub to a specific set of actions, even if the token has broader access. With these limitations, if the agent is compromised through prompt injection, its permissions remain confined to that repository, with no credential available to steal.

"The problem with giving AI agents autonomy is that we've been giving them authority they don't actually need," said Ariadne Conill, fellow and co-founder of Edera. "An agent might need permission to update one repository or execute one command, but that shouldn't require handing it credentials that open the door to an entire environment. Object capabilities let us separate the action from the authority behind it, so agents can do useful work without becoming a security liability."

Existing security tools can isolate workloads, manage secrets, or monitor agent behavior, but they often leave applications holding credentials or operating with permissions broader than their immediate tasks require.

body: Teams describe a business flow such as checkout or invoice approval in plain English. An AI browser agent walks it in a real browser, and Siemba's DAST engine tests only the endpoints that flow touches, with no Selenium scripts to record or maintain.

The capability is built for the question every release raises, "Is the flow we just changed still safe?" Teams describe the flow in plain English, an AI browser agent navigates it in a real browser, and Siemba's DAST engine tests only the endpoints that flow uses. Findings are tied to the scenario and build that produced them, and a saved scenario can be rerun on every build with consistent, comparable results.

Why full scans and recorded scripts fall shortA full DAST scan crawls every reachable page and tests every endpoint it finds. That breadth has value, but it answers the wrong question after a targeted release. In a large application with hundreds of modules owned by different teams, a change to payments triggers testing of the HR portal and help center too. Crawlers follow links, so they often never reach deep flows like a refund page that only appears after an order is placed, paid and delivered. And a whole-application findings list leaves the team digging for the answer that matters to their release.

The usual workaround is to record a browser session in a tool such as Selenium and upload the script to the scanner. Recorded scripts replay fixed selectors, so a renamed button, a new modal or a redesigned form breaks them. Over time the scripts go unmaintained, and scoped testing quietly stops.
How Business Scenario Testing worksA scenario goes from a single sentence to a scoped, repeatable security test in four steps, with the team in control at each decision point:

What automation covers, and what it does notBusiness Scenario Testing finds technical vulnerabilities, such as injection and misconfiguration, inside flows a crawler might never reach. Advanced logic-abuse flaws, such as reusing a one-time coupon or skipping a payment step, depend on application-specific rules that scanners cannot judge. Siemba covers those cases through expert-led penetration testing on the same platform. The capability complements full-application scans rather than replacing them: full scans provide breadth, and business scenarios provide depth on the flows that carry the most risk.

The Llica-to-Uyuni route sits at approximately 3,700 metres above sea level, close to the 3,776-metre summit elevation of Mount Fuji. At that altitude, each breath delivers about 35 percent less oxygen than at sea level. The route has approximately 311 metres of positive elevation gain.

Fernanda Maciel started at 05:00 on September 28, 2026, beneath the arch in Llica on the western side of the salt flat. Maciel navigated by phone along the route Leonardo used in 2023. A hailstorm had turned sections of the Salar de Uyuni into shallow water and mud, with hidden water-filled holes beneath the surface. Around kilometre 145, Maciel crossed a series of pools and stopped to change shoes and socks.
Maciel's stomach began to struggle with food after the first 100 kilometres, and Maciel did not follow a fixed target pace.
"I had to adapt my legs to a pace where my body was comfortable running 170 kilometres at altitude in a desert," Maciel said.

body: When Aura was founded in 2017, it set itself one goal: to build a constant, trusted protector that watches out for families online, protects them autonomously and brings people in only when it matters.

For forty years, security software asked people to do the work: run the scan, read the alert, figure out what it meant, fix it themselves. Aura set out to build the alternative, and over eight years assembled everything an intelligent system needs to see—identity, credit, bank and card activity, devices, children, data brokers, calls and texts—reaching millions of families at home, through partnerships with schools worldwide and through employer benefits.

The stakes have risen along the way. Generative AI has made scams cheaper to run and harder to spot, and cybercrime losses have reached a record $20.9 billion. Software that answers with another alert cannot keep up.

Two things remained out of reach, because the technology to build them did not exist: a mind that could learn what normal looks like for one particular family and tell a real threat from a false alarm, and hands that could act for that family across the accounts, carriers and devices where safety actually happens. Solstice is the engine that provides both.

"When we started Aura, we set ourselves the goal of building a protector that does the work for you and brings you in when it needs you," said Hari Ravichandran, Founder and CEO of Aura. "Setting the goal was the easy part. The hard part was building the intelligence to understand a family and the agents to act for it, and that took nearly a decade, our own data and our own models, including a proprietary foundation model. We named the engine Solstice for the point in the year when the light turns. This is that point for consumer security: from software that warns you to a system you can ask to take care of it."
Solstice is an engine, not a feature. It is the foundation under every Aura product, and it has five parts.

body: Existing DLP tools rely heavily on regex rules and predefined policies, generating false positives while missing sensitive data that employees have renamed, compressed, or otherwise disguised. They often lack visibility into what people are doing with data as it moves between files, applications, and destinations. Separate insider risk tools can identify unusual behavior, but an action that falls outside someone's normal routine does not necessarily pose a security risk. An employee using a new application for the first time, for example, may trigger an anomaly without putting any sensitive information at risk. Security teams need to understand what data is involved, how it is being used, and whether the activity serves a legitimate business purpose before determining whether an incident requires attention.

Bold addresses these problems through AI that runs directly on the endpoint. Its Data Classification Engine uses small language models to understand sensitive information based on meaning and context. The new Intent Engine builds on that capability by tracking how data moves, identifying attempts to disguise sensitive information, and analyzing user activity against established behavioral patterns. It evaluates these signals alongside data sensitivity, business context, and the potential consequences of an action to determine whether an activity presents a meaningful risk, whether it results from legitimate work, employee negligence, or deliberate misuse.

"DLP has always struggled to distinguish between someone doing their job and someone putting sensitive data at risk," said Nati Hazut, Co-Founder and CEO of Bold Security. "An employee can do something unusual without creating a security problem, while another employee can follow a familiar workflow that exposes confidential information. AI gives us the ability to understand the data and the circumstances surrounding an action, so security teams can focus on activity that actually matters. Intent Engine brings that context together in a single DLP solution."
Intent Engine introduces three capabilities that work together with Bold's existing on-device AI data classification technology.

Together, these capabilities allow Bold to assess risk based on the data involved, the actions taken, and the context in which they occur. A user might accidentally expose sensitive information through an otherwise routine workflow, while another might deliberately disguise confidential data before transferring it outside the organization. Intent Engine helps identify both scenarios without treating every deviation from normal behavior as evidence of malicious intent. Security teams can review incidents with the relevant data classification, file history, user context, and explanation of the risk, rather than piecing together evidence from separate DLP and insider risk management systems.

"An unusual action doesn't necessarily mean someone is stealing data, and a routine action doesn't mean the data is safe," said Hadar Krasner, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer of Bold Security. "Someone might deliberately try to hide sensitive information, accidentally send it somewhere they shouldn't, or simply use a new tool to get their work done. Those situations carry very different levels of risk. Intent Engine looks at the data, the behavior, and the business context together so security teams can understand what actually requires their attention."

On June 13, 2026, Nara Organics recalled all of its Whole Milk Organic Infant Formula — every lot and both can size after federal and state health officials linked the product to a multistate outbreak of infant botulism. According to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), three infants in California, Pennsylvania, and Washington, ranging in age from two to five months, were sickened with type A botulinum toxin, with illness onset between April and May 2026. All three babies were hospitalized and treated with BabyBIG®, the antitoxin produced by the California Department of Public Health.
The recalled formula was manufactured in Germany and sold only in the United States — nationally, through Target stores, Target.com, and Nara.com — between July 2025 and June 2026.

This is the second infant-formula botulism outbreak in seven months. In November 2025, ByHeart Whole Nutrition Infant Formula — also made from whole milk powder — was tied to an outbreak that the FDA reported sickened approximately 48 infants across 17 states. That outbreak, and the nationwide recall and FDA warning letters that followed it, were public months before the Nara babies in this outbreak became ill.

The lawsuit alleges that, by the time Nara Organics was still manufacturing, distributing, and selling its whole-milk formula in the spring of 2026, the danger was no longer hypothetical. Years earlier, on March 8, 2023, the FDA issued a formal Call-to-Action letter to the infant-formula industry that named Clostridium botulinum by name and identified whole milk powder as a potential vehicle for contamination. The science was not in dispute: botulinum spores survive ordinary pasteurization and the spray-drying used to make powdered formula, and they can take hold in an infant's gut and produce a paralytic toxin.

The global facade systems market is expected to grow significantly, driven by rapid urbanization, increased construction of commercial, residential, and high-rise buildings, and a growing focus on energy-efficient building envelopes. The facade is no longer just an architectural finish. It is a performance component that governs thermal insulation, daylight access, acoustic comfort, weather resistance, and a building's overall energy consumption. As buildings account for a large share of global energy use and emissions, developers and regulators are paying closer attention to the envelope to reduce operating energy demand. Stricter green building codes and certifications, such as LEED, BREEAM, and IGBC, are encouraging the use of advanced glazing, insulated panels, and ventilated facade solutions. Developers are also adopting unitized and prefabricated systems to shorten construction timelines, reduce reliance on on-site labor, and improve installation quality. Advances in low-emissivity glass, lightweight composites, smart and dynamic facades, building-integrated photovoltaics, and BIM-based design tools are improving performance and enabling complex architectural designs. Growing renovation and retrofit activity, rising demand for sustainable buildings, and expanding infrastructure and real estate development are expected to further support market growth.
Curtain walls are expected to be the second-fastest-growing type segment during the forecast period.

Curtain walls are expected to be the second-fastest-growing type in the global facade systems industry over the forecast period, driven by rising construction of high-rise commercial and mixed-use buildings in dense urban centers. A curtain wall is a non-structural cladding assembly, typically aluminum-framed with glass or metal infill, that carries only its own weight and transfers wind and lateral loads to the primary structure. This makes it well suited to tall buildings, where lighter facades reduce structural and foundation requirements. Its large, glazed areas also maximize natural daylight, improve occupant well-being, and deliver the sleek, modern look developers favor for premium properties. Growing demand for energy-efficient envelopes is further supporting adoption. Modern curtain walls incorporate thermally broken frames, double and triple glazing, and advanced coatings that improve thermal, acoustic, and weather performance. Unitized and prefabricated systems are reducing on-site labor and installation time, helping contractors meet tight schedules. Rising investments in office towers, hotels, airports, and retail complexes are expected to further drive growth.

Kerr; Frederick County Executive Jessica Fitzwater; Frederick County Council President Brad Young; City of Frederick Mayor Michael O'Connor; Maryland Tech Council Chairman Brad Stewart; and members of Theradaptive's leadership team. Guests toured the new facility following the ribbon cutting.

"This facility marks an important milestone for Theradaptive, and we're proud to build our future in Frederick," said Dr. Luis Alvarez, Founder and CEO of Theradaptive. "Commercial biomanufacturing of OsteoAdapt in-house, alongside the team that developed it, gives us direct control over quality, timelines, and supply as we move toward commercialization. This expansion will also power our pipeline expansion into next-generation protein therapeutics based on our platform technology. We're grateful to our state, county, and city partners, and to our team, for making this possible."

The new facility places R&D and manufacturing side by side, and targets kilogram-scale cGMP bioproduction to meet projected commercial demand, while keeping supply chain control, newly developed manufacturing methods, and intellectual property in Maryland. The expansion lays the groundwork for organizational and physical growth over the next five years, creating skilled biomanufacturing, quality, and engineering jobs in Frederick County.

"Monocacy 1 is the step that ultimately turns our process from clinical-scale to commercial-ready," said Ed Fix, Vice President of Manufacturing at Theradaptive. "Just as important, we're building the quality systems and manufacturing expertise here in Frederick that commercial supply will depend on."

This investment is supported in part by a grant from the Maryland Department of Commerce's Build Our Future Grant Program, part of Governor Wes Moore's Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023. In June of 2026, Theradaptive was one of 11 organizations selected statewide for this round of funding, which supports the reshoring of critical manufacturing processes and the acquisition and setup of equipment for commercial-scale cGMP production of OsteoAdapt. Theradaptive's growth in Maryland has also been supported by multiple awards from the Maryland Stem Cell Research Fund (MSCRF), including Manufacturing Assistance funding that helped establish cGMP manufacturing in Frederick and Clinical Award funding that is supporting OsteoAdapt clinical studies. Monocacy 1 at Theradaptive's headquarters in Frederick, Maryland sits in a federal Opportunity Zone the U.S. Treasury designated under OZ 2.0.

OsteoAdapt SP is Theradaptive's lead investigational therapeutic, powered by AMP2™, a proprietary rhBMP-2 variant engineered to promote targeted, sustained bone regeneration. By minimizing off-target effects and addressing key limitations of current graft materials, OsteoAdapt SP aims to meaningfully improve both the safety and efficacy of spinal fusion.

title: Brazil's Tobacco Health Cost Recovery Lawsuit Reaches Critical Milestone as Court Prepares to Rule
excerpt: A landmark lawsuit filed in 2019 by Brazil's Office of the Attorney General (Advocacia-Geral da União, or AGU) seeking to hold the country's...
lede: Statement of Yolonda C. Richardson, President and CEO of Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Brazil's represents a significant milestone in verifiable regulation infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Statement of Yolonda C. Richardson, President and CEO of Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids

The lawsuit seeks to require the country's largest cigarette manufacturers to compensate Brazil's public health system for healthcare expenditures related to diseases scientifically linked to tobacco use. The defendants include BAT Brasil (formerly Souza Cruz) and Philip Morris Brasil, and their parent companies, British American Tobacco and Philip Morris International.

The case is one of the world's most significant tobacco health cost recovery lawsuits and could have implications far beyond Brazil. If successful, the case would reinforce the principle that tobacco companies should be held accountable for the enormous health and economic costs caused by their products.

Tobacco use imposes an enormous burden on Brazil's public health system. Each year, smoking causes approximately 177,000 deaths and costs an estimated R$75 billion (almost US$15 billion) in healthcare expenditures to treat tobacco-related diseases. The lawsuit argues that although the manufacture and sale of cigarettes are lawful activities, companies remain legally responsible for compensating society for the damages caused by their products.

Brazil's lawsuit is the first of its kind in a low- or middle-income country to reach a liability ruling. Similar health cost recovery actions have been pursued in other countries, including Canada and the United States, where governments have successfully sought compensation for healthcare expenditures attributable to tobacco use.

The tobacco industry has caused enormous and well-documented public health harm in Brazil. A favorable ruling would not only represent a major milestone for Brazil but will also establish an important precedent for governments seeking to hold the tobacco industry accountable.

The information is used to generate a detailed 3D model that appraisers can review and verify. Depending on loan eligibility and applicable requirements, the process may support an appraisal waiver or allow an appraiser to use Automax.ai's suite of AI-powered tools to complete the appraisal report.

body: "The economy is about to gain 10 billion new participants, and none of them are human," said Sinclair Toffa, co-founder and CEO of Mural. "Our mission has been to connect people and businesses to the Global Financial Internet. Now we are connecting agents as well."

Mural serves as a single system to manage the accounts, payments, identity, and compliance behind financial products designed for humans and the agents authorized to act on their behalf, handling the licenses, bank relationships, and local and blockchain payment rails required to operate across markets. Customers, including Deel, Opera, and Axexo, use Mural to build financial products such as payroll and remittance workflows, enabling their end users to hold dollars, stablecoins, and local currency in a unified account. These accounts have a policy and compliance engine that lets both people and agents securely store money and transact globally, with controls such as account limits, approved counterparties, and custom approvals on larger payments. Since launching its API in 2025, Mural has processed $2.1 billion in payment volume for end users in 128 countries. Its 2026 volume to date is nearly six times its total for all of 2025.

Many global businesses stitch together dozens of financial tools, bank partners, and compliance vendors to offer financial products to their customers. As these systems scale, so do the complexities of managing the components and policies of a user's financial accounts across platforms and providers. Stablecoins and agents are making the problem more acute. Real-world stablecoin payments more than doubled in 2025 to roughly $390 billion, with businesses accounting for about 60%, according to McKinsey and Artemis Analytics, and businesses are now accepting payments from AI agents. When an agent moves money, businesses need to know who authorizes it and who is accountable if it goes wrong.

As engineers at Palantir, Mural's founders, Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, worked alongside Fortune 100 companies to integrate various independent systems that were built for different functions. Now, they are solving the same problem for the growing number of software companies that are adding financial products with more capabilities, more providers and more systems operating around the same customer with nothing to connect them. The problem of disjointed systems only intensifies as companies begin connecting agents to their platforms.
Mural brought Palantir's forward-deployed model to finance: its engineers embed with customers on the ground in each market and launch the integration alongside them.

body: Dr. Kali Spoto LaRue explains how early physical therapy supports recovery, mobility, strength, and a safer return to athletic activity.

The article explains that athletes throughout Fairport and Greater Rochester often face uncertainty about when to begin treatment after an injury. Whether the injury occurs during school sports, recreational exercise, or competitive training, the timing of physical therapy can influence both recovery progress and long-term performance. According to the article, beginning physical therapy earlier often helps athletes heal more safely while reducing the risk of future complications.

A sports injury can affect more than the injured area itself. The HelloNation article notes that pain, swelling, and movement limitations frequently change how athletes walk, run, lift, or perform routine activities. These movement changes, known as compensation patterns, can place additional stress on muscles and joints throughout the body. Physical therapy helps identify these patterns early before they contribute to further discomfort or delayed recovery.

The article describes how one of the first goals of physical therapy after a sports injury is evaluating how the injury affects the quality of movement, strength, balance, flexibility, and mobility. During the initial appointment, therapists review the mechanism of injury, symptoms, medical history, and activity demands related to the athlete's sport or training routine. This information helps create a personalized recovery plan that matches both the athlete's condition and performance goals.

Many athletes assume they should wait until pain completely disappears before starting treatment. However, the article explains that delaying physical therapy can sometimes allow stiffness, weakness, and reduced mobility that become harder to correct later. Early physical therapy often includes controlled movement and gentle exercises that encourage healing while protecting the injured area from unnecessary strain.

The HelloNation article further explains that physical therapy programs are adjusted based on the severity and type of sports injury involved. Athletes recovering from sprains, muscle strains, tendon injuries, or surgical procedures may all require different approaches that take into account tissue healing principles and the athlete's unique situation. Therapists monitor progress closely throughout recovery to ensure exercises remain safe and appropriate during every stage of treatment.
