The Business Activity Index remained in expansion territory in May, increasing 1.8 percentage points to 57.7 percent from April's reading of 55.9 percent. The New Orders Index registered 57.3 percent, 3.8 percentage points above April's figure of 53.5 percent and 2.6 percentage points higher than its 12-month average reading of 54.7 percent. The Employment Index contracted for the third month in a row with a reading of 47.9 percent, a 0.1-percentage point decrease from the 48 percent recorded in April; of the four subindexes that make up the composite PMI®, it is the only one that remains below its 12-month moving average," says Miller.

"The Supplier Deliveries Index registered 55.2 percent, 1.6 percentage points lower than the 56.8 percent recorded in April. This is the 18th consecutive month that the index has been in expansion territory, indicating slower supplier delivery performance. (Supplier Deliveries is the only ISM® PMI® Reports index that is inversed; a reading of above 50 percent indicates slower deliveries, which is typical as the economy improves and customer demand increases.)

"The Prices Index increased to 71.3 percent in May, 0.6 percentage point above April's figure of 70.7 percent and recording its highest reading since August 2022 (72.6 percent). The index has exceeded 60 percent for 18 straight months, increasing its 12-month average from 67.7 percent to 68 percent. Diesel, gasoline, oil and related commodities were once again most frequently mentioned as up in price in May.

"The Inventories Index registered 62.5 percent, up 9.4 percentage points from April's figure of 53.1 percent and equaling May 2010 as its highest reading since Services PMI® data collection began in 1997. The Inventory Sentiment Index expanded for the 37th consecutive month, registering 55.2 percent, up only 0.1 percentage point from April's figure of 55.1 percent. The Backlog of Orders Index remained in expansion territory for a fourth straight month, registering 51.3 percent in May, down 1.7 percentage points from the April figure of 53 percent; this is the index's third consecutive decrease from February's reading of 55.9 percent. The New Export Orders and Imports indexes both remained at 50 percent or above for the fourth month in a row. The New Export Orders Index decreased by 2.1 percentage points from 52.1 percent in April to 50 percent in May, and the Imports Index registered 51.1 percent, a decrease of 3.6 percentage points compared to its April reading of 54.7 percent. Both the New Export Orders and Imports indexes registered above their 12-month moving averages.

"Seventeen industries reported growth in May, three more than in April, and the number reporting contraction dropped to one, a decrease of two from April. The May Services PMI® reading of 54.5 percent is 1.7 percentage points above the 12-month average of 52.8 percent. That average is an uptick of 0.3 percentage point over April's 12-month average of 52.5 percent."

body: The number of closed sales in Northern Virginia totaled 1,152 in October, a 19.5% decrease from October 2025. Nationally, home sales declined 8.8% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million. The larger decline in Northern Virginia points to a more significant contraction in local transaction activity compared to the national market, suggesting that local sales activity faced greater headwinds during the month.

"October's numbers illustrate how Northern Virginia's housing market is adjusting at a different pace than the national market," said NVAR CEO Ryan T. McLaughlin. "While higher inventory is giving buyers more opportunities than they had a year ago, specifically in the attached homes market, that additional supply has not yet translated into stronger sales activity. Even with more homes available, affordability challenges and borrowing costs may be influencing the pace of buyer activity."

Despite the slowdown in sales, home prices remained relatively stable. Northern Virginia's median sold price was $750,500 in October, a marginal 0.07% increase from October 2025. The national median sold price was $416,700, up 0.4% year over year. Both markets recorded modest price gains, indicating that the slower pace of sales has not resulted in significant downward pressure on home values. Northern Virginia's higher median price also reflects the region's distinct housing market and price structure.

Homes in Northern Virginia spent an average of 29 days on the market in October, up 3.6% from the same month last year. Nationally, days on market increased 6.0% to 35 days. Although days on market lengthened both locally and nationally, Northern Virginia homes continued to sell six days faster than the national average. This difference indicates that buyer activity in Northern Virginia, while slower than a year ago, remains more steady compared to the broader national market.

Available inventory continued to be one of the most significant differences between the two markets. Northern Virginia had 3,505 active listings in October, a 30.8% increase compared to October 2025. Nationally, active listings totaled 1.59 million, representing a 4.6% year-over-year increase. The growth in Northern Virginia inventory was more than six times the national rate, demonstrating a substantially larger expansion in the number of homes available to local buyers. The increase was once again driven by townhomes and condos, creating more options for buyers in the market for an attached home.

Months of supply provides another measure of the difference between local and national market conditions. Northern Virginia recorded 2.6 months of supply in October, a 30.0% increase from October 2025. Nationally, months of supply reached 5.1, up 15.9% year over year. Although supply increased at nearly twice the national rate in Northern Virginia, the region still had approximately half the inventory supply available nationally. This comparison underscores that, despite substantial local inventory gains, Northern Virginia remains a tighter market with fewer homes available relative to the pace of sales.

body: At Singapore FinTech Festival, Bybit's Chief Legal & Compliance Officer highlighted the importance of practical use cases, regulatory alignment and operational safeguards.

Speaking at the SFF Future Matters Stage session, "Building Trusted Hubs for Programmable Money," Peter shared his views on the challenges facing programmable finance, including the need to establish clear user demand, improve coordination across regulatory frameworks and build trust through sound operational practices.

Peter said the development of programmable money and tokenisation should start with a clear understanding of the problems they aim to solve. Technology alone is not a reason to develop a new financial product. Firms should first establish whether a solution meets a genuine market need, offers practical benefits to users and delivers something that existing financial services cannot.
Regulatory alignment can improve the payment experience

Peter highlighted the complexity of payment transactions, which can involve four to six regulated entities operating under different regulatory frameworks. Each institution may have its own risk appetite, transaction monitoring requirements and fraud prevention measures. These differences can create delays or interruptions, even when the payment process appears straightforward to users.

He called for greater clarity on standards across the payment chain, covering technical requirements, on-chain and off-chain activities, transaction values, monitoring practices and fraud controls. A risk-based approach remains important, but better alignment could help reduce friction while maintaining appropriate safeguards.

title: OpenAssets and Sui Advance Institutional Tokenization Standards Under Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust
excerpt: OpenAssets, a leading digital asset infrastructure provider, today announced a collaboration with Sui to advance the development of the Open...
lede: OpenAssets and Sui set to collaborate on developing OTAS, an open, agnostic standard hosted by LF Decentralized Trust that defines how tokenized asset systems can seamlessly connect to the Sui ecosystem.
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from OpenAssets represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: OpenAssets and Sui set to collaborate on developing OTAS, an open, agnostic standard hosted by LF Decentralized Trust that defines how tokenized asset systems can seamlessly connect to the Sui ecosystem.

Institutions are increasingly issuing tokenized versions of securities, funds, commodities, and other assets, with projections putting the tokenized asset market at $30 trillion by 2034, according to Standard Chartered. Those assets often remain locked inside separate, incompatible systems, and connecting them has historically required time-consuming, expensive custom integration work for every chain involved.

OTAS is designed as a neutral, auditable foundation for identity, compliance, asset representation, and reporting, one institution can build on rather than adopt wholesale. The collaboration focuses on making tokenized financial assets interoperable, meaning they can be moved and verified across different networks without the need for expensive, custom-built software for every single chain. With OTAS available on Sui, assets issued in the Sui ecosystem follow the same open rules as assets on other networks, so their history and status can be trusted wherever they move.

OTAS is an open standards lab hosted at Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT), initiated by OpenAssets and sponsored by Sui Foundation, which joined LFDT in September 2026. The lab was formally added to LFDT in Spring 2026, and includes open source smart contract reference implementations for tokenized financial instruments.

Neutral, shared standards have repeatedly helped emerging technology markets scale. The Linux Foundation has spent more than two decades helping build trusted, vendor-neutral governance for technologies including Linux, Kubernetes, and PyTorch. OpenAssets, a Premier Member of LF Decentralized Trust, proposed OTAS to bring that same model of open governance to tokenized capital markets.

"Extending OTAS to Sui makes compliance and ownership history portable, giving institutions a consistent, trusted view of an asset across networks," said Gabor Gurbacs, Chairman and CEO of OpenAssets. "We welcome Sui's contribution to OTAS and the broader effort to build open, interoperable standards for tokenized assets."

body: After a review of the determination as requested by Greenbrier, CBP again determined that there was substantial evidence that Greenbrier evaded paying duties on the FRCs from Mexico and China entering the United States. Despite importing FRCs covered by AD/CVD orders, CBP noted that, in submissions to CBP, Greenbrier conceded that it did not formally declare or file entry documentation and did not tender AD/CVD cash deposits or duties for the mounted FRCs.

Instead, Greenbrier improperly claimed that its railcars, and the FRCs attached, were exempt from formal entry and duties. CBP concluded that Greenbrier failed to file required entry documentation, constituting a material omission, and also failed to tender applicable AD/CVD cash deposits and duties for the covered merchandise, resulting in evasion.

"CBP's decision is an important reaffirmation of EAPA's purpose to ensure compliance with U.S. antidumping and countervailing duty laws and to prevent evasion of lawfully owed duties," said Daniel B. Pickard, lead counsel for the Coalition of Freight Rail Coupler Producers. "It also helps protect the domestic industry from unfair trade practices by sending a clear message that U.S. trade laws will be enforced."

As a result of CBP's affirmation, CBP will require formal entries for the FRCs subject to the applicable AD/CVD orders, including requiring Greenbrier to file formal consumption entries for the railcars to which the FRCs are affixed. Greenbrier will also be required to rectify non-compliance with provisions governing admission of railcars carrying FRCs during the relevant period of investigation. CBP also recognized that its decision does not preclude CBP or other agencies from pursuing additional enforcement actions or penalties.

title: FocalPoint extends S-GNSS® to physical AI platforms dependent on reliable positioning
excerpt: FocalPoint today announced the expansion of its S-GNSS® technology into the smart cities and robotics markets, extending its positioning...
lede: Proven in automotive, S-GNSS® now extends to smart cities and mobile robotics, from delivery drones to micromobility platforms.
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from FocalPoint represents a significant milestone in verifiable crypto casinos infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Proven in automotive, S-GNSS® now extends to smart cities and mobile robotics, from delivery drones to micromobility platforms.

The expansion addresses a common challenge across these applications: maintaining reliable positioning in challenging environments. In cities, tall buildings reflect satellite signals, creating multipath that degrades accuracy. Under thick foliage and around other obstacles, satellite signals can be weakened or obstructed. Receivers are also increasingly vulnerable to jamming and spoofing. And the compact form factor of many robotic platforms often leaves antennas poorly placed.

FocalPoint's Supercorrelation® signal processing addresses these challenges at the GNSS receiver level. It improves accuracy in multipath-heavy environments, strengthens resilience to spoofing and jamming, and helps recover performance where antenna placement is compromised. It works with existing receiver hardware, with no additional sensors required.

As location-aware systems become increasingly autonomous, reliable positioning is fundamental to navigating their surroundings, supporting location-based services and operating safely around people. A delivery robot deciding which way to cross or a robotaxi receiving false positioning information from a spoofer must make decisions based on the information available to it. There is no driver to catch the error.

S-GNSS® is already established in automotive and is available commercially as a firmware upgrade through FocalPoint's collaboration with STMicroelectronics. S-GNSS® Auto is integrated with ST's Teseo GNSS receivers, bringing enhanced positioning performance to autonomous driving applications. The expansion into smart cities and robotics extends FocalPoint's technology to new markets facing similar GNSS reliability challenges.

"Physical AI is moving out of controlled environments and into the real world, where reliable positioning becomes essential to what these systems can achieve," said Scott Pomerantz, CEO of FocalPoint Positioning. "Our technology gives autonomous systems a sharper understanding of where they are, helping them navigate complex environments safely. We're excited to bring our years of experience in automotive to this next generation of intelligent machines."

The milestone was reached during CFBNJ's inaugural "Meal on a Mission: A Chef's Tableside Experience," held on June 12 at Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Atlantic City. The event brought together community leaders, acclaimed chefs, local businesses and supporters committed to addressing food insecurity throughout South Jersey.

"Meal on a Mission is a powerful example of what can happen when the Atlantic City community comes together around a common goal," said George Goldhoff, president, Casino Association of New Jersey (CANJ). "Through our partnership with the Community FoodBank of New Jersey, Atlantic City's casino industry is helping to create a meaningful, lasting impact for our families facing food insecurity throughout our region."

During Meal on a Mission, the Atlantic City casino industry collectively donated nearly $120,000 to CFBNJ. This included a $50,000 donation from the CANJ, along with a $50,000 donation from Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Atlantic City in honor of its eighth anniversary. The inaugural event was made possible by Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Atlantic City as Host and Culinary Visionary Sponsor, CANJ as Culinary Visionary Sponsor, Caesars Entertainment Atlantic City as Executive Chef Sponsor, and Borgata Hotel, Casino & Spa and Ocean Casino Resort as Epicurean Sponsors. Chefs and restaurants from Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa, Caesars Entertainment Properties, Golden Nugget Atlantic City, and Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Atlantic City participated in the event.

Casinos Unite Against Hunger is a collaborative initiative launched in May 2025 by the Atlantic City casino industry in partnership with the Community FoodBank of New Jersey to address food insecurity in communities across South Jersey. In addition to financial support, casino employees have volunteered with CFBNJ initiatives and participated in community outreach efforts. During the 2025 holiday season, the industry participated in a mobile food pantry in Ventnor and helped provide 1,200 turkeys to families in need. In 2026, in addition to sponsoring Meal on a Mission, Caesars Entertainment Atlantic City donated $20,000 to support the CFBNJ, and the MGM Resorts Foundation donated $10,000.

"Every day, too many individuals and families around New Jersey face difficult choices between paying bills, keeping a roof over their heads, and putting food on the table," said Elizabeth McCarthy, President & CEO of the Community FoodBank of New Jersey (CFBNJ). "We are incredibly grateful for the support of organizations like the Casino Association of New Jersey as we work to eliminate hunger in the Garden State."

Those with the highest score in each category receive the "Best of Innovation" distinction. An elite panel of industry expert judges, including members of the media, designers, engineers and more, reviewed submissions.

An ultra-light multi-sport robot, Aura delivers voice-guided cues, builds customizable match-like drills, and generates individualized performance reports on technique, consistency, movement, and progress. Combining robotics, computer vision, machine learning, Aura makes data-driven coaching accessible - and is able to track every serve, spin and rally, turning each session into measurable feedback that accelerates skill development and performance.

A three-sport machine, Aura's internal design accommodates three different ball types while maintaining stable performance. Pongbot reworked the hardware architecture so a single mechanical launch-wheel system can automatically adjust its spacing and acceleration parameters for each ball type. The result is a lightweight 8.9 kg machine that one person can carry, load into a car, and take straight to the court—without sacrificing its multi-sport capabilities.

"We're honored to receive this award and thank CTA and the judges for recognizing Aura's unique ability to combine adaptive ball-delivery hardware with AI-powered visual analysis and coaching into one machine able to accommodate different sports. This recognition celebrates our team's hard work and our commitment to building technology that makes a meaningful difference for our customers," said Haibo Zhang, CEO of Pongbot.

title: Solana Foundation Launches Solana DvP, an Atomic Settlement Program Built for Financial Institutions
excerpt: Solana Foundation, a non-profit dedicated to the decentralization, growth, and security of Solana, today announced Solana DvP, an open-source...
lede: Released under the MIT license, it aims to bring the settlement certainty that banks and other financial institutions require to public blockchain infrastructure for the first time as a reusable standard that is atomically settled, provides isolated escrow, and enforces deadlines.
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Solana Foundation represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Released under the MIT license, it aims to bring the settlement certainty that banks and other financial institutions require to public blockchain infrastructure for the first time as a reusable standard that is atomically settled, provides isolated escrow, and enforces deadlines.

J.P. Morgan provided Solana Foundation with valuable input on institutional settlement practices and requirements. The result combines J.P. Morgan's decades of securities settlement expertise with Solana's performance as the leading venue for tokenized real-world assets. Until now, institutional trades settling onchain have typically relied on bespoke smart contracts. Solana DvP replaces that with one standard rail.

"Atomic settlement removes counterparty risk that is inherent in traditional finance. Solana DvP program provides institutions with one open standard across the Solana ecosystem, on public infrastructure, with finality in seconds instead of days." – Catherine Gu, Head of Product, Digital Assets, Solana Foundation.

"A shared, open standard for atomic delivery-versus-payment is exactly the kind of foundational infrastructure institutional market participants require to operate at scale without introducing settlement risk and counterparty exposure. We were pleased to contribute our settlement expertise." – Rhodel D'souza, Head of Markets Digital Assets, J.P. Morgan.

Delivery-versus-payment is the bedrock of securities settlement: it ensures the asset and cash move simultaneously to eliminate principal risk. Traditional markets achieve this through a multi-day chain of clearinghouses, depositories, and custodians, tying up capital for one to two days. Solana DvP hopes to compress that process into a single atomic transaction: both legs settle together, or neither does, with finality in seconds rather than days.

The program is meant for the assets institutions can hold. Solana DvP supports SPL Token and Token-2022, including the extensions regulated issuers depend on — like permanent delegate, pausable tokens, and transfer hooks. Any two counterparties can use it with any settlement agent — a bank, a custodian, an exchange. J.P. Morgan's feedback helped shape the program to meet institutional requirements from day one. The result is an open standard that anyone can adopt, build on, and use.

body: The revised terms, filed in an amended registration statement on Form S-4 with the SEC, adjust the number of shares issuable to investors at closing based on the value of XRP at that time, as measured by its volume-weighted average price, rather than the XRP price of $2.36 used when the business combination agreement was signed. By tying share issuance to a more current value of XRP, the company's capitalization is expected to more closely reflect the value of its underlying treasury at closing.

"Tying the share count to XRP's value at closing is the right thing to do for Evernorth and our investors," said Asheesh Birla, founder and CEO of Evernorth. "We're preserving alignment among investors while supporting our long-term strategy of building institutional access to the XRP ecosystem. That our entire advance funding group stands behind it, in this environment, reflects their continued conviction in our strategy and the opportunity ahead."

Evernorth's investors subscribed through a series of private placements, most funding in advance and others on a delayed basis, at $10.00 per share. While the restructured transaction reflects XRP's market value at closing rather than the XRP price used at signing, the company's strategy remains unchanged. Addressing the difference up front allows public investors to gain exposure at the time of the planned listing on terms better aligned to the net asset value underlying each share, rather than a valuation based on historical XRP prices.

Because the transaction is better aligned with XRP's underlying value, the restructuring is expected to reduce the number of shares issued at closing, spreading the company's net asset value across fewer shares so that each share represents a larger portion of Evernorth's XRP treasury. The adjustment mechanism works in both directions based on XRP's value at the time of closing. All of Evernorth's advance funders agreed to the revised terms, which are intended to improve alignment among stakeholders and better position the company for its public market debut. Consistent with this approach, the Armada II sponsor has agreed to adjust its founder shares on the same proportional basis as the advance funding investors, ensuring that the impact of the restructuring is shared broadly across stakeholders. Management and Evernorth's founding investors believe the amendment will result in a capitalization structure that more accurately reflects the value of the company's underlying XRP holdings at closing.

Evernorth's investors include Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR, among others. The company's holdings and strategy remain the same. It will be building XRP per share over time through disciplined capital allocation, XRP ecosystem participation and treasury operations.

excerpt: Why do growing businesses still struggle with cash flow? HelloNation answers that question in an article featuring insights from Accounting...

expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from HelloNation represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: The article explains how stronger cash flow planning helps businesses avoid common financial setbacks and make more confident decisions.

HelloNation answers that question in an article featuring insights from Accounting Expert Kimberly Furrh of Furrh & Associates PC in Lawton, OK. The article explains that strong sales alone do not guarantee financial stability and that understanding cash flow is essential for supporting sustainable business growth.

The HelloNation article explains that many business owners mistakenly assume higher revenue automatically improves business cash flow. In reality, revenue and available cash are not always the same. A business may record income when an invoice is issued, but delayed customer payments can leave the company without enough cash to cover everyday expenses. Understanding business cash flow helps owners recognize potential challenges before they begin affecting operations.

According to the article, one of the most common obstacles to effective cash flow management is late customer payments. When invoices remain unpaid, businesses may need to postpone purchases, delay investments, or rely on credit to meet routine obligations. The article notes that monitoring accounts receivable, maintaining consistent billing practices, and following up on overdue invoices can improve collections while supporting healthier cash flow management.

The article also discusses how rising operating expenses gradually affect business cash flow. Costs such as payroll, rent, utilities, insurance, and inventory often increase over time, making them easy to overlook until they begin affecting profitability. Regular financial reviews allow business owners to identify expense trends early and make informed adjustments before small issues become larger financial concerns.

Another important recommendation is preparing realistic cash flow forecasting. Looking only at a company's current bank balance provides an incomplete picture of its financial position. The article explains that cash flow forecasting helps estimate future income and expenses while preparing for seasonal changes, tax obligations, equipment purchases, or slower business periods. Regular cash flow forecasting provides valuable insight that supports more informed financial decisions.

body: The prospective, single-arm, pre-market study will enroll up to 300 patients in Europe and Australia with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis caused by severe calcium buildup in the aortic valve. The study will be the basis to seek approval for use in Europe and Australia.

"TAVI has transformed the treatment of severe aortic stenosis, but physicians continue to seek technologies that make procedures more predictable and allow treatment to be tailored to individual patients," said Didier Tchétché, M.D., director of the structural heart disease department, Clinique Pasteur, Toulouse, France, and co-principal investigator of VOYAGER CE. "Encantor's balloon-expandable design and software-guided approach are intended to give physicians greater control and procedural confidence."
Encantor designed to treat narrowing of aortic valve

Aortic stenosis occurs when calcium builds up in the aortic valve – which controls the flow of oxygen-rich blood to the body – and causes it to narrow. Eventually, the heart must work harder to pump blood through the narrowed valve. Left untreated, it can lead to heart failure and death.

The investigational Encantor system works by crimping the new heart valve on a deflated surgical balloon. The balloon with the mounted valve is then inserted into the body and guided through a catheter in an artery in the groin to the heart. Once properly positioned inside the diseased aortic valve, software-guided deployment helps customize expansion of the valve to the patient's unique anatomy for a more precise fit. Once the new valve is in place, it takes over the function of the patient's damaged native valve. The balloon is then deflated and removed from the body.

Continued research and expansion of TAVI solutions is key as the needs of physicians and patients evolve. Leveraging insights from physicians, the latest technology advancements and key learnings from the company's Navitor™ TAVI product portfolio, Abbott developed the differentiated Encantor TAVI platform to enhance procedural ease of use and controlled, precise deployment, while offering optimal blood flow (hemodynamics) through the valve.

Miller a récemment fondé GamReg Consulting, un cabinet de conseil spécialisé dans la réglementation des jeux d'argent, après avoir passé dix ans au sein de la Commission des jeux d'argent du Royaume-Uni, où il occupait dernièrement le poste de directeur exécutif chargé des politiques et de la recherche. GCI sera l'un des premiers clients de Miller dans le cadre de cette nouvelle aventure, où ce dernier travaillera en étroite collaboration avec Matt Holt, directeur général de GCI, ainsi qu'avec son équipe afin d'apporter son point de vue d'ancien responsable de la réglementation. Dans cette nouvelle fonction, Miller aura pour mission de soutenir les efforts d'expansion de GCI sur les marchés internationaux, de veiller à ce que les solutions de GCI répondent aux besoins en constante évolution des autorités de réglementation des jeux d'argent, et d'éclairer le développement des produits sous l'angle réglementaire. Miller enrichira également de son expérience des politiques réglementaires et de sa vision stratégique les conseils que GCI délivre à ses clients du secteur réglementaire qui s'emploient à répondre aux besoins de leurs citoyens.

Depuis sa création en 2025, GCI propose une gamme de services aux autorités de réglementation des jeux d'argent du monde entier, notamment des plateformes de surveillance des transactions et d'informations sur le marché parmi les plus performantes du secteur. Dans le contexte de la Coupe du monde 2026, GCI a fourni aux autorités de réglementation des analyses de surveillance du marché, afin de les aider à mieux cerner l'activité globale des paris sur leur territoire, qu'elle soit le fait d'opérateurs agréés ou non. Dans un seul État américain, GCI a recensé plus de 2 000 opérateurs en activité, dont la grande majorité ne détenait aucune licence.

« Alors que GCI ambitionne de devenir le fournisseur de référence des autorités de réglementation des jeux d'argent du monde entier en ce qui concerne les informations sur le marché, l'arrivée de Tim Miller, avec ses compétences et sa réputation, montre à ces autorités que nous comprenons les défis auxquels elles sont confrontées, et que nous mettons en place les outils et les services qui les armeront mieux que jamais pour les relever », déclare Matt Holt, directeur général de GCI. « Nous avons suivi de près le travail accompli par Tim au cours de la dernière décennie au sein de la Commission des jeux d'argent du Royaume-Uni, et nous sommes ravis de le voir désormais jouer un rôle essentiel pour construire l'avenir de GCI. »

« Au moment où je lance GamReg Consulting, il est tout à fait logique que je m'associe à l'équipe de GCI, qui propose aux autorités de réglementation les outils dont elles ont besoin pour obtenir des informations sur le marché », commente Tim Miller, conseiller stratégique de GCI et fondateur de GamReg Consulting. « Je sais par expérience que les outils dont les autorités de réglementation ont besoin pour protéger leurs citoyens ne cessent d'évoluer, et je veillerai à ce que GCI et ses clients gardent une longueur d'avance dans l'optimisation de leurs marchés. »

Holt et Miller interviendront lors du salon Global Gaming Expo (G2E) à Las Vegas, à l'occasion de la table ronde intitulée « De nouveaux outils pour une nouvelle ère : aider les autorités de réglementation à comprendre les dynamiques du marché et à lutter contre les jeux d'argent illégaux ». La table ronde aura lieu le mercredi 30 septembre à 14 heures (heure du Pacifique), dans la salle Titian 2305 du Venetian Expo à Las Vegas. Aux côtés de Holt et Miller, on retrouvera Oliver Shawano, vice-président de la Commission des jeux d'argent des Potawatomi du comté de Forest, Stéphanie Maxwell, directrice adjointe du Conseil des paris sportifs du Tennessee et conseillère juridique en son sein, ainsi que Jonathan Michaels, fondateur de Michaels Strategies.

Same Pattern Holds Across Cannabis, Gambling, Crypto, Supplements, Telehealth, and Every Other Restricted Commercial Category.

The Index measures retrieval-layer treatment of 15 brands across four AI engines — ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews — scored on a six-metric rubric producing a composite AI Visibility Score 0–18 per brand per engine.

The central finding — what the report calls "the Naming Threshold" — documents that AI engines surface restricted-category brands when those brands are named in the prompt, but route around the entire category when users ask the same underlying question in generic terms. The query "best creator subscription platforms 2026" returns Patreon, Beehiiv, Substack, and Stan Store. The query "OnlyFans alternatives for creators" returns Fansly, Fanvue, ManyVids, JustForFans, FanCentro, and LoyalFans. Same engine. Same underlying need. Two different brand universes.

Tests were conducted in May 2026 in fresh sessions across the four engines, with personalization disabled, U.S. locale, English language. Six metrics scored 0–3 each: Citation Share, Refusal Rate, Sentiment, Factual Accuracy, Brand Confusion, Source Quality. All ownership, financial, and regulatory facts referenced in the report are drawn from publicly reported sources including Variety, Bloomberg, the Financial Times, Time, CNN, Ars Technica, 404 Media, EFF, Wikipedia, and UK Companies House filings.

The Restricted Category AI Visibility Index is the first in an Everything-PR Index family covering AI-engine treatment of major commercial verticals. Volume 2 — expanding to 25 brands, 12 prompt categories, and 5 engines — is scheduled for January 2027.

Global contributory networks detected over 95,000 fraud events tied to a single abuse network, representing an exposure of up to $3.2 million.

Fraud is most concentrated at the beginning and end of the customer journey, specifically during account creation and withdrawals which accounts for roughly 60% of total fraud exposure. While direct financial losses remain the most visible consequence, operators also report rising compliance costs, customer churn and brand damage as key areas of impact.

"Bonus abuse has become the gaming industry's version of first-party fraud," said Sean Britt, senior director, global gaming markets, LexisNexis Risk Solutions. "It's organized, repeatable and difficult to detect without multi-layered intelligence. As gaming operators compete for players through incentives and faster onboarding, they must also strengthen their defenses at the point of entry."

Despite mounting threats, the report finds that North American gaming professionals remain focused on frictionless user experiences. Eighty one percent (81%) of respondents said even moderate onboarding friction can drive customers to competitors, prompting increased investment in automated KYC processes and real-time fraud detection tools.

The study also reveals that data collaboration is an underused yet powerful defense: Only one in five operators currently share fraud intelligence, though those that do report faster detection, fewer false positives and improved customer trust.

As online gaming operators continue to navigate the dual pressures of delivering seamless player experiences while combating increasingly sophisticated fraud networks, the industry's path forward will depend on smarter, more collaborative defenses. The findings from the report make clear that bonus abuse is not just a financial risk but a structural challenge that demands coordinated action, advanced intelligence and a renewed focus on trust.

body: "An overnight trade does not end when it is executed, firms also need the people, controls and technology to monitor exceptions and support the trade through settlement," said Quentin Limouzi, Global Head of Post Trade at Broadridge. "Broadridge's systems are operational during extended trading hours. As demand grows, the market won't wait for the back office to catch up."

"Extended trading hours could give investors more opportunities to respond to events and access U.S. markets," said Steve Byron, Managing Director and Head of Technology, Operations and BCP at SIFMA. "But a resilient market depends on more than an open trading window. The industry must work together to understand the implications for liquidity, operations and the infrastructure that supports investors around the clock."

The October 2026 survey of 268 financial institutions points to a central tension: the ability to execute an overnight trade does not necessarily mean the services, controls and operational coverage around it are ready to operate continuously.

Demand is not simply a question of adding more time to the trading day. Respondents identified the ability to trade overnight and to react to geopolitical events as leading objectives. At the same time, only 10% expected liquidity to be adequate for institutional-size execution from day one, suggesting a selective early market rather than an immediate shift of all trading activity.
Firms should assess their readiness across people, processes and technology now, and engage providers to address the operational gaps that extended trading hours may expose.

The ValueExchange conducted the global industry survey in October 2026 in partnership with SIFMA and Broadridge. It includes views from 268 financial institutions on the potential impact of near-23-hour trading, five days a week, and firms' preparations. Figures reflect respondents' expectations and plans, not observed outcomes.

body: In a 55-page opinion issued November 6, 2026, Judge Robert W. Gettleman of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois denied the defendants' motion to dismiss J-MM's claims under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO). The court also denied the defendants' motion to strike under California's anti-SLAPP statute and their request for attorneys' fees.

J-MM alleges that Simmons Hanly, using Sokolove as a source of referrals, pursued asbestos claims against the company through fabricated exposure narratives, scripted product-identification testimony, and concealed bankruptcy-trust claims in order to extract settlements. The court described the action as alleging "an extensive scheme devised by lawyers and firms to defraud plaintiff through serial lawsuits based on false testimony and concealed information."

The court rejected the defendants' argument that litigation activity can never constitute racketeering. It held that the First Amendment-based Noerr-Pennington doctrine does not require dismissal at this stage, because J-MM's allegations, if proven, would fall within the exception for sham lawsuits and intentional misrepresentations. The court also declined to dismiss the RICO claims as untimely.

"The court has allowed our racketeering claims against Simmons Hanly, its leadership, its lawyers and its referral partner, Sokolove Law, to move forward," said Lisa Carteen, General Counsel of J-MM. "It recognized that litigation conduct is not automatically immune from federal racketeering law when it is part of a scheme built on false testimony and concealed evidence. J-MM has always defended asbestos claims on their merits, and we look forward to proving our claims. Our fight is about restoring integrity to asbestos litigation, so that compensation goes to the people who were truly harmed."

"This is an important ruling for any company that has faced serial sham claims under the cover of litigation," said Ashwin J. Ram of Buchalter LLP, counsel for J-MM. "The court rejected the argument that a law firm's litigation conduct can never be racketeering activity and declined to dismiss the case on First Amendment petitioning grounds. The case now moves into discovery, where J-MM will be able to examine how these claims were generated, investigated, and brought."

The court dismissed J-MM's state-law claims without prejudice under California's litigation privilege. The RICO claims, which provide for treble damages and attorneys' fees, will proceed against all named defendants, who must answer the complaint by December 7, 2026.

LYMPHIR is a targeted immunotherapy for relapsed or refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) indicated for use in Stage I–III disease after at least one prior systemic therapy. It is a recombinant fusion protein that combines the IL-2 receptor binding domain with diphtheria toxin (DT) fragments. The agent specifically binds to IL-2 receptors on the cell surface, causing DT fragments that have entered cells to inhibit protein synthesis, resulting in cell death. Denileukin diftitox-cxdl has demonstrated the ability to deplete immunosuppressive regulatory T lymphocytes (Tregs) and antitumor activity through a direct cytocidal action on IL-2R-expressing tumors. LYMPHIR was approved by the FDA and subsequently launched in the U.S. in December 2025.

Citius Oncology, Inc. (Nasdaq: CTOR) is a platform to develop and commercialize novel targeted oncology therapies. In December 2025, Citius Oncology launched LYMPHIR, approved by the FDA for the treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory Stage I–III CTCL after at least one prior systemic therapy. Management estimates the initial CTCL market for LYMPHIR currently exceeds $400 million, is growing, and is underserved by existing therapies. Robust intellectual property protections that span orphan drug designation, complex technology, trade secrets, and pending patents for immuno-oncology use as a combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors would further support Citius Oncology's competitive positioning. In December 2025, Citius Oncology launched LYMPHIR, a targeted immunotherapy for the treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory Stage I–III CTCL who had had at least one prior systemic therapy. excerpt: TÜV SÜD officially released the White Paper on Capability and Performance Grading for Grid Forming Energy Storage Units and Systems. TÜV SÜD...
lede: Grid-Forming Energy Storage Is Evolving Toward System Support, and a Unified Framework for Capability Evaluation Is Urgently Needed
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Huawei represents a significant milestone in verifiable regulation infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Grid-Forming Energy Storage Is Evolving Toward System Support, and a Unified Framework for Capability Evaluation Is Urgently Needed

The proportion of renewable energy and power electronics devices in power systems continues to increase. As a result, new technology-based resources must gradually take over the inertia, voltage support, power oscillation damping, and other stability capabilities provided by traditional synchronous generators. Grid-forming energy storage systems integrate energy regulation with active grid-support capabilities. They are evolving from traditional energy storage devices into important stability resources for new power systems.

At the same time, different devices vary significantly in support scope, dynamic performance, islanding operation, and system restoration. The industry urgently needs a clear evaluation framework to answer "what grid-forming capabilities are available, what level they can reach, and how much system responsibility can be taken on."
Five-Level Grid-Forming Capability System: Making System Contributions Measurable and Verifiable

The newly released white paper proposes a five-level grid-forming capability maturity model, from L0 to L4. This model centers its evaluation on the actual contributions of devices and plants to the power system. It also clearly defines the capability evolution path from traditional grid-following through local voltage grid-forming, regional auxiliary grid-forming, and conditional full-domain grid-forming, to advanced full-domain grid-forming. The evaluation focus has expanded from whether a single function is available to the coverage of capabilities, performance levels, verification levels, and contributions to system resilience. This enables evidence-based assessment of different grid-forming capabilities and the selection of appropriate levels for varying application requirements.

The white paper focuses on core capabilities such as grid formation, frequency support, voltage support, system strength support, and fault support. Considering factors such as response speed, support strength, and operating boundaries, it drives grid-forming evaluation from functional descriptions toward measurable performance verification. It also extends verification requirements from individual devices to plants.

body: "Reliable measurement is fundamental to a healthy digital advertising marketplace, but the legal frameworks supporting those relationships have often been shaped one agreement at a time," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "By developing a common contractual foundation for measurement services, we're giving the industry a practical starting point that can reduce friction, improve efficiency, and help organizations spend less time negotiating custom agreements and more time delivering value for all."

The Measurement Services Addendum is the latest component of IAB's modular legal framework, building on the General Terms v1.1 and Direct Buy Addendum v1.0 released earlier this year. Designed for use by advertisers, agencies, publishers, media owners, platforms, and measurement providers, the framework establishes standardized terms for advertising measurement relationships, helping reduce contractual fragmentation, streamline negotiations, improve operational efficiency, and create greater consistency across the digital advertising ecosystem while remaining flexible enough to accommodate different technologies, methodologies, and business models.

"Measurement has become increasingly sophisticated, but the contracts governing those services haven't kept pace," said Cintia Gabilan, SVP, Centers of Excellence & Industry Initiatives, IAB. "The Measurement Services Addendum gives organizations a practical legal framework they can adopt as written or incorporate into existing agreements, making it easier to create greater consistency across measurement relationships while accommodating different business models and technologies."

The public comment package includes the Measurement Services Addendum v1.0, General Terms v1.1 and Appendix 1 – Definitions v1.1, which together establish a shared legal baseline for advertising measurement relationships. The General Terms are incorporated by reference into the addendum and are intended for use with an applicable addendum rather than as a standalone agreement.

IAB invites advertisers, agencies, publishers, platforms, measurement providers, ad technology companies, and legal, procurement, finance, privacy and ad operations professionals to review the draft and provide feedback. Comments received during the public comment period will be considered in the finalization process.

Public comments will be accepted through October 22, 2026. Feedback, including suggested edits, implementation questions, and general usability comments, may be submitted to [email protected]. Draft documents are available here.

body: La scale-up italiana ha nominato Turnbow per guidarne l'espansione tecnica nell'intelligenza artificiale e nel calcolo ad alte prestazioni, con un approccio energy-to-compute volto a sfruttare le fonti di energia rinnovabile e riutilizzare le risorse esistenti per sviluppare nfrastrutture di calcolo più sostenibili.

L'accesso all'energia elettrica è uno dei principali vincoli per lo sviluppo delle infrastrutture per l'IA. Secondo i dati di Terna al 31 agosto 2026, le richieste di connessione alla rete dei data center in Italia hanno superato complessivamente i 100 GW, rispetto ai circa 30 GW della fine del 2024. Un aumento che rende cruciali la scelta dei siti e i tempi necessari per la connessione alla rete.

L'approccio energy-to-compute di ALPS si basa su una scelta precisa: ubicare i data center dove l'energia è già disponibile, anche al di fuori dei principali hub, per ridurre la dipendenza dalle aree congestionate della rete. La società intende integrare fonti di energia rinnovabile e riqualificare siti industriali dismessi, riutilizzando, ove tecnicamente possibile, le connessioni alla rete, gli edifici e altre risorse esistenti. L'obiettivo è sviluppare infrastrutture di calcolo più sostenibili, sfruttando le risorse locali e, attraverso il riutilizzo delle strutture esistenti, limitando il consumo di suolo e riducendo la necessità di nuove costruzioni. Questa espansione si affianca alle attività di mining già svolte da ALPS, che proseguono in linea con il piano aziendale.

Turnbow guiderà la strategia tecnica di ALPS per l'IA e l'HPC, dalla valutazione delle architetture e dei siti fino al confronto con i partner tecnologici e industriali. L'Italia sarà un mercato prioritario. ALPS intende riportare in Italia le proprie competenze internazionali e collaborare con imprese italiane del settore ingegneristico e industriale, avvalendosi anche della loro esperienza in progetti realizzati all'estero.

"L'Italia e l'Europa dispongono di risorse energetiche, infrastrutture industriali e competenze tecniche che possiamo sfruttare", afferma Francesco Buffa, CEO e cofondatore di ALPS. "Attraverso il nostro approccio energy-to-compute, vogliamo trasformare il potenziale energetico e industriale delle regioni in cui operiamo in un vantaggio competitivo e contribuire a ridurre il divario dell'Europa nel campo dell'IA."

Turnbow vanta oltre 25 anni di esperienza nei settori delle telecomunicazioni e delle infrastrutture digitali e ha ricoperto ruoli tecnici presso TWT, Unidata e CDLAN. Fa parte del consiglio direttivo di ITNOG.

body: As of September 3, 2026, the Company's combined cash, restricted cash and Bitcoin holdings totaled approximately $53 million, based on a Bitcoin price of approximately $81,500, representing nearly 200% of the Company's equity market capitalization as of that date.

Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data, stated, "Hyperscale Data currently holds approximately $36 million in cash and restricted cash and approximately 215 Bitcoin, with an estimated market value of approximately $18 million. Together, these assets total approximately $53 million, equal to nearly twice the Company's recent equity market capitalization.

"We sold a portion of our Bitcoin and deployed the proceeds to support the continued buildout of our Michigan AI data center as we prepare to perform under our master services agreement (the 'MSA') with a California-based neocloud provider. The MSA provides for the deployment of 20 megawatts, has an initial term of 10 years and includes two five-year extension options that may be exercised by the customer. If the customer exercises both extension options, the MSA is expected to generate in excess of $1.2 billion in revenue over the maximum 20-year term.

"This was a deliberate capital-allocation decision. We believe investing in the infrastructure necessary to perform under the MSA has the potential to create substantially greater long-term value for the Company and our stockholders. Even after deploying capital toward the Michigan facility, the value of our cash, restricted cash and remaining Bitcoin substantially exceeds our recent equity market capitalization. Although this comparison does not reflect our liabilities or the restrictions applicable to certain cash balances, we believe it provides meaningful context regarding the Company's current market valuation and underlying assets. In my view, the market is not presently reflecting the underlying value of the Company."

The Company notes that the market value of Bitcoin and the market capitalization of Hyperscale Data fluctuate continuously. Restricted cash is subject to applicable restrictions on its use. The comparison in this release is intended to highlight the relationship between these specific assets and the Company's recent equity market capitalization and should not be interpreted as a calculation of net cash, enterprise value, liquidation value or amounts available for distribution to stockholders.

Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center that offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Hyperscale Data's other wholly owned subsidiary, Ault Capital Group, Inc. body: "New Mexico's Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham and Attorney General Raúl Torrez are blatantly and unconstitutionally enforcing New Mexico's seven-day waiting period law, despite it having twice been held to violate Second Amendment rights of law-abiding New Mexicans," stated Lawrence G. Keane, NSSF's Senior Vice President & General Counsel. "Criminals do not purchase firearms at retail and do not submit to a waiting period before illegally obtaining a gun. This unconstitutional law only impacts law-abiding citizens seeking to exercise their constitutional rights to purchase and possess a firearm for lawful purposes. Twice now federal courts have ruled this law is unconstitutional. It is outrageous that the governor and attorney general are still moving ahead to enforce an unconstitutional law. It is a grotesque misuse of government power, a waste of taxpayer money and puts law-abiding citizens at risk while doing nothing to punish criminals. NSSF is confident we will be victorious in court."

Last year, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit ruled in an NSSF-supported challenge Ortega v. Grisham that New Mexico's seven-day waiting period for firearm purchases infringes on the Second Amendment by preventing the lawful acquisition of firearms by those who had already passed a NICS check. The case was remanded to the district court which, citing the Tenth Circuit's decision, granted summary judgment and entered a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing the law as to the named plaintiffs. Despite these rulings, the state is appealing again and has said it will enforce this unconstitutional law. NSSF has been on the frontline of this legal challenge, funding the initial appeal and remand proceedings, as well as the opposition to the state's new appeal.

It is NSSF's position that the Tenth Circuit was clear that the law is unconstitutional as to all individuals who receive a "proceed" from NICS and strongly disagrees with the state's threat to enforce this unconstitutional law against federally licensed firearm retailers who are not a party to the original case. It is regrettable that NSSF and its litigation partners have no choice but to file a second lawsuit to ensure that its members are protected.

Formed in 1961, NSSF has a membership of thousands of manufacturers, distributors, firearms retailers, shooting ranges, sportsmen's organizations and publishers nationwide. body: As small businesses increasingly seek integrated technology experiences, ADP and PNC are bringing payroll, HR, banking and payments together through a new offering, PNC Payroll by ADP®. The new offering helps reduce operational complexity, making it easier for small businesses to manage critical needs like cash flow, payments, compliance and payroll.

"Small businesses want technology that works together seamlessly," said Matt Farwell, president of Small Business Services at ADP. "This collaboration brings together two of the systems small businesses rely on most: banking and payroll. With decades of combined expertise supporting businesses through critical financial and payroll decisions, ADP and PNC are uniquely positioned to provide a trusted, centralized platform that can ultimately help business owners spend less time navigating disconnected systems and more time focusing on growth."

"Our clients rely on us for the tools and support they need to build and grow their businesses," said Dave Shorten, head of SMB Treasury Management at PNC Bank. "This collaboration combines ADP's small business expertise and scalable solutions with PNC's relationship-driven approach to banking, creating a powerful solution that supports small businesses at every stage of growth."

Bringing Payroll, HR and Banking Together Small businesses traditionally manage payroll, HR and banking activities across multiple systems. PNC Payroll by ADP brings those functions together in a single workflow. By embedding ADP's AI-enabled payroll and HR capabilities into PNC's digital experience, businesses can manage critical operations with greater confidence and accuracy.

PNC Payroll by ADP will give small business banking customers access to payroll, HR, time tracking, insurance and retirement solutions directly through their digital banking platform. The offering is designed to support businesses as they grow, from startups and one-person operations to more established companies looking to scale. Built on ADP's experience serving more than 900,000 small businesses, the solution was purposefully designed to address their needs, combining simplicity and expert support.

PNC Payroll by ADP will combine digital self-service capabilities with access to 24/7 live ADP payroll experts. ADP brings more than 77 years of experience helping businesses manage payroll and navigate the federal, state and local requirements that affect the workplace. AI-powered capabilities help automate routine tasks while ADP's payroll experts provide the guidance businesses need to effectively pay and manage their people.

body: With more buyers than sellers in the market, bankers are weighing lending team liftouts in pursuit of growth, according to the 2027 Bank M&A Survey.

According to the survey, 35% of bank executives and directors say their bank is very likely or somewhat likely to make a whole bank acquisition in 2027, down from 45% who said the same a year earlier. Two-thirds of potential acquirers cite a lack of suitable targets as a top barrier to making a deal, and the percentage who say their board and management team would be open to selling for the right price in the next five years fell slightly to 46%.

"While it's possible that some bank boards could be swayed by an attractive price or the potential upside of a combination, many prefer to remain independent," says Patrick Vernon, strategy and transaction advisory partner with Crowe. "There are still plenty of opportunities to grow independently — from expanding into new business lines or markets to improving profitability."

Without suitable targets, some banks may settle for poaching talent instead. Thirty-five percent of bank leaders believe it is very or somewhat likely their bank will lift out a lending team, an increase of 11 percentage points from a year ago. Banks have also seen indirect gains from consolidation: 62% say their institution picked up customers as a result of in-market consolidation in 2025 or 2026.

"It's not only the buyer and seller that benefit in an acquisition," says Emily McCormick, vice president of editorial & research at Bank Director. "Not everyone wants to stay with a bigger institution. Bank leaders should have a game plan for picking up dissatisfied clients and talent."

We wanted to invest in a place that already meant something to this community and give local athletes and families a home field they can be proud of."

The improvements include nearly 980,000 square feet of new AstroTurf across six rebuilt baseball fields. Unrivaled Sports also restored and reinforced the replica outfield walls, replaced the perimeter home run netting, and completed extensive landscaping, pedestrian, technology, and infrastructure upgrades. Nigro Construction renovated approximately 6,000 square feet of restaurant space across two restaurants. New Unrivaled Sports Park signage and wayfinding complete the park's updated look.

The result is a park designed to serve two roles: a reliable, high-quality home field for Las Vegas athletes, coaches, and families, and a destination capable of bringing regional and national tournaments, teams, and visitors to the city.

"Gary Reese Freedom Park is a regional outdoor space that serves the entire Las Vegas valley and Ward 3," Mayor Pro Tem Olivia Diaz said. "We will continue to invest and add new amenities for use by our residents, and the multi-million-dollar improvements by Unrivaled to the existing sports park area bring this facility to the next level. I look forward to families enjoying everything it has to offer, especially our young athletes."

Unrivaled Sports has worked closely with the City of Las Vegas throughout the transformation, meeting regularly with city leaders on improvements to the park and ways the property can continue serving the surrounding community. body: Vyhlásenie Yolondy C. Richardsonovej, prezidentky a generálnej riaditeľky organizácie Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids (Kampaň za deti bez tabaku)

Žaloba sa požaduje od najväčších výrobcov cigariet v krajine, aby kompenzovali brazílskemu systému verejného zdravotníctva náklady na zdravotnú starostlivosť v súvislosti s chorobami vedecky prepojenými s užívaním tabaku. Medzi žalovanými sú spoločnosti BAT Brasil (predtým Souza Cruz) a Philip Morris Brasil ako aj ich materské spoločnosti British American Tobacco a Philip Morris International.

Tento prípad je jedným z najzásadnejších súdnych sporov o náhradu nákladov na zdravotnú starostlivosť v súvislosti s tabakom na svete a mohol by mať dopady aj ďaleko za hranicami Brazílie. V prípade úspešnosti by prípad podporil zásadu, že tabakové spoločnosti by mali niesť zodpovednosť za obrovské zdravotné a ekonomické náklady spôsobené ich výrobkami.

Užívanie tabaku predstavuje pre brazílsky systém verejného zdravotníctva obrovskú záťaž. Každoročne fajčenie spôsobuje približne 177 000 úmrtí a náklady na zdravotnú starostlivosť na liečbu chorôb spojených s tabakom sa odhadujú na 75 miliárd realov  (takmer 15 miliárd USD). Žaloba tvrdí, že hoci sú výroba a predaj cigariet legálne činnosti, spoločnosti zostávajú zo zákona zodpovedné za kompenzáciu verejnosti za škody spôsobené ich výrobkami.

Brazílska žaloba je prvou svojho druhu v krajine s nízkymi alebo strednými príjmami, kde bude vynesené rozhodnutie o zodpovednosti. Podobné opatrenia na úhradu nákladov na zdravotnú starostlivosť boli prijaté aj v iných krajinách vrátane Kanady a Spojených štátov, kde vlády úspešne žiadali o kompenzáciu výdavkov na zdravotnú starostlivosť, ktoré možno pripísať užívaniu tabaku.

Tabakový priemysel spôsobil na verejnom zdraví v Brazílii obrovské a dobre zdokumentované škody. Kladné rozhodnutie by predstavovalo významný míľnik nielen pre Brazíliu, ale zároveň dôležitý precedens pre vlády, ktoré sa snažia brať tabakový priemysel na zodpovednosť.

Seit seiner Gründung im Jahr 2016 arbeitet Flutterwave daran, den Geldtransfer zwischen den verschiedenen Finanzmärkten Afrikas zu vereinfachen. Durch die Verknüpfung lokaler Zahlungsmethoden, Banknetzwerke und internationaler Zahlungssysteme über eine einzige Plattform hilft das Unternehmen Unternehmen dabei, Zahlungen zu akzeptieren, neue Kunden zu erreichen und über Grenzen hinweg zu expandieren. Im Laufe des letzten Jahrzehnts hat sich Flutterwave zu einer Finanztechnologieplattform entwickelt, der rund vier Millionen Privatpersonen und Unternehmen vertrauen – von kleinen und mittleren Unternehmen bis hin zu globalen Organisationen. Das Unternehmen hat mehr als eine Milliarde Transaktionen im Wert von über 50 Milliarden US-Dollar abgewickelt, was den Umfang seiner Geschäftstätigkeit und die wachsende Nachfrage nach zuverlässiger, interoperabler Finanzinfrastruktur auf dem gesamten Kontinent widerspiegelt.

Olugbenga 'GB' Agboola, Gründer und CEO von Flutterwave, sagte: „Von Euromoney als Afrikas bester Zahlungsinfrastrukturanbieter ausgezeichnet zu werden, ist ein stolzer Moment für alle bei Flutterwave, insbesondere da wir unser zehnjähriges Jubiläum feiern. Als wir Flutterwave im Jahr 2016 gründeten, war es unser Ziel, afrikanischen Unternehmen den Geldtransfer und die Teilnahme an der Weltwirtschaft zu erleichtern."

Anfang dieses Jahres wurde Flutterwave von CNBC und Statista als eines der 250 besten Fintech-Unternehmen der Welt ausgezeichnet, während Gründer und CEO Olugbenga Agboola vom Fintech Magazine zu einem der 100 führenden Fintech-Unternehmen ernannt wurde. While Rain offers the convenience of an end-to-end platform, its infrastructure is also built to be open and interoperable. body: "This study shows that, contrary to popular belief, gamblers are financially savvy entertainment consumers – especially sports bettors who demonstrate a particularly high level of financial literacy and mathematical capability," said David Forman, American Gaming Association's Vice President of Research. "Prediction market" users tend to overestimate their mathematical skillset, often thinking they are better at mathematical reasoning than they actually are, unlike traditional sports bettors who have a more accurate self-assessment.

"The research highlights the risks of "prediction markets" marketing sports betting as investing against "peers" and the dangers of misleading consumers into thinking they just have to be smart to win," Forman stated.

The gap between "prediction market" users' confidence and demonstrated mathematical ability raises significant consumer-protection concerns. Consumers who are led to believe they have an analytical "trading" advantage may underestimate or misjudge the risks. Presenting sports wagers as investments and a money-making strategy compound the danger by encouraging users to believe they can outsmart what are often sophisticated counterparties they are led to view as peers.

"As we close out another Responsible Gaming Education month, this research also identifies a potential link between responsible gaming and financial literacy, laying the groundwork for future research into this important topic," said Forman. "It reinforces the principle that gambling must be promoted – and approached – as what it is: a form of entertainment, not a financial strategy."

The researchers conducted a national online survey of 3,201 U.S. adults through Prolific from July 15–21, 2026. Following data-quality screening, the final sample included 3,149 participants: 537 sports bettors, 574 prediction market users, 557 casino players, 495 iGaming users and 986 non-gamblers. The survey has a margin of error of plus or minus two percentage points at the 95 percent confidence level.

The American Gaming Association commissioned the research. Colin López, Ph.D., founder and principal of IN Research & Analytics LLC, and Jackson Sears, Ph.D., founder and principal of Matrix Consulting Group of North Carolina, conducted the research and analysis. Both are co-founders of the Betting, Experience, and Trading in Sports (BETS) Research Center and an assistant professors at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

body: The brief in Kenneth W. Lathrop, et al. v. Thor Motor Coach, et al., supports consumers challenging provisions in a Thor Motor Coach warranty that directed disputes to Indiana and selected Indiana law. The Court of Appeal, Second Appellate District, Division Seven, refused to enforce those provisions in a published 2024 decision, and Thor sought review in the Supreme Court.

After the consumers challenged those provisions, Thor offered not to oppose the application of two California statutes — the Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act and the Consumers Legal Remedies Act — in the Indiana proceeding while continuing to insist that the case be sent there. The consumers objected to the proposed stipulation and never signed it. The brief argues that companies should not be allowed to insert unlawful terms into consumer contracts and then offer to abandon only part of those terms in the rare case where a consumer successfully challenges them.

"Companies should not be allowed to bury illegal terms in a form contract, count on consumers to follow them, and then retreat only when the rare consumer has the resources to fight back," said William Pletcher, Litigation Director for Consumer Watchdog. "A right the Legislature has declared unwaivable must be real for every consumer—not just those savvy enough to disregard the contract, hire California counsel and challenge it in court."

California's Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act and Consumers Legal Remedies Act provide important warranty and consumer-protection rights. Both laws declare that any contractual waiver of the rights and remedies they confer is contrary to public policy and void.

The brief argues that Thor's proposed approach would leave behind the consumers most likely to be harmed by unlawful contract terms: those who believe what the contract says. Consumers may file in the designated out-of-state forum without asserting their California rights, or may abandon relatively small claims because litigating across the country appears too difficult or expensive. In this specific case, Indiana's lemon law does not cover motor homes, so a California buyer who follows the contract to Indiana may find no comparable remedy there — and may never learn that California law guaranteed one.

"Thor's proposed rule would turn unlawful contract drafting into a largely risk-free strategy," Pletcher said. "Most consumers will believe the contract or simply give up. The company changes course only when someone catches it—and even then wants to keep the benefit of forcing the case across the country. California law should not reward that kind of trap."

body: The exhibition, organized by The New-York Historical Society, highlights the contributions of the only six women employed as full-time photographers by LIFE magazine between the late 1930s and early 1970s out of 101 photographers on staff during its run as a weekly publication. At a time when photojournalism was largely dominated by men, these photographers documented defining moments in American history, captured significant social and political changes, and brought compelling human stories to millions of readers.

"These six remarkable women helped shape the way generations of Americans experienced and understood the world through photography," said Dr. Daryl Ward, executive director of The AGB. "Their work not only documented pivotal moments in history but also challenged conventions in a profession where women were often overlooked. We are proud to bring this important exhibition to Central Florida and share their extraordinary contributions to photography and journalism with our community."

First presented in New York in 2019, the exhibition explores the way Americans saw the world through the lens of photographers at LIFE, the first magazine in the United States to tell stories with images rather than text. These innovative photo essays became the hallmark of the publication. The exhibition provides context to this unique storytelling format through published and unpublished photographs, including vintage prints, copy prints and contact sheets. In addition, the photographs show the editing process behind the final published stories that helped define the United States as a world power during what Henry Luce, LIFE founder and editor-in-chief, called the "American Century." This is the first exhibition to focus on the six women who worked as full-time photographers for LIFE.

LIFE: Six Women Photographers was curated by Marilyn Satin Kushner, former curator and head of the Department of Prints, Photographs, and Architectural Collections, as well as Sarah Gordon, curatorial scholar in women's history, with Erin Levitsky of Ryerson University and William J. Simmons, former Andrew Mellon Foundation Pre-Doctoral Fellow at the Center for Women's History.

The exhibition is proudly sponsored by Northern Trust. Generous support is provided by Joyce B. Cowin, with additional support from Lara Lee Schupf, Jerry Speyer, and Robert A.M. Stern. This exhibition has been organized by The New-York Historical Society.

Through this investment, both companies aim to address one of global finance's biggest challenges. Cross-border payments still depend on banking hours, correspondent networks, and capital tied up in pre-funded accounts, slowing trade and raising costs for businesses and their customers. Stablecoins settle in minutes, around the clock, freeing up liquidity and lowering the cost of moving value between markets. SCRYPT makes this simple in practice for institutions: fiat in, stablecoins across the border, fiat out. A commodity trader can settle with a counterparty in another time zone the same day, not when both banks next open. body: The physical world and human biology are dynamic open systems. According to industry estimates, 85% of global GDP resides in the physical world. According to UN DESA estimates, the global population reached 8.3 billion in 2026, all of it exposed to environmental factors from prenatal development onward.

Today's LLMs see little of this. The combinatorial space of environmental exposures dwarfs any existing training corpus, including those of frontier LLMs by several orders of magnitude. More than 200 million chemical substances have been cataloged, over 350,000 are registered for commercial production and use, and each can act on a genome of 3.1 billion base pairs. Of the genome's roughly 28 million CpG sites, about a fifth (5–6 million) change methylation state across cell types, and many more may respond to exposures over a lifetime.
Jumptuit's Physical World Intelligence: Built to Observe, Not Just Read

The Anticipatory Intelligence Framework draws on Jumptuit's Live Data Conduit, made up of Global Data Nets (GDNs) and Global Sensory Intelligence (GSI). The LDRM applies multi-mode reasoning (e.g, sign, comparative, causal, analogical, temporal, verbal), dynamic cross-sector threshold driven curiosity queries and urgency drivers to detect anomalies and track how variables change over time. The architecture is supported by the Jumptuit Group's growing USPTO patent portfolio, including the recently granted U.S. Patent No. 12,793,535.
The framework is built on aggregated, de-identified environmental and public data, with privacy, consent and human oversight by design.

"The limits of genomic research alone, and of Large Language Models, come from the same gap - neither can observe the physical world as it changes," said Donald Leka, Founder, Chairman and CEO of the Jumptuit Group. "Our Anticipatory Intelligence Framework is designed to close that gap, so researchers can see the invisible interactions that precede disease and disruption."

While 84 percent of manufacturers report benefits from artificial intelligence, only 20 percent of AI use cases have successfully scaled.1 At the same time, the equipment powering critical sectors such as data centers, water infrastructure and food production remains one of the largest untapped sources of operational intelligence.

By turning motor data into actionable insights, ABB Intelleqt helps customers improve reliability, increase productivity and identify energy saving opportunities of 30 percent or more3. Dado que hasta un 62 %* de los equipos informan haber enviado a sus clientes documentos de transacciones y modelos financieros que contenían errores generados por IA, resulta aún más crucial revisar eficazmente dicha documentación. Deck Check AIR utiliza IA generativa para auditar la precisión de todas las diapositivas de una presentación de PowerPoint; va más allá del formato para detectar errores de cálculo e incoherencias lógicas que perjudican la credibilidad. La herramienta se diseñó específicamente para revisar documentos financieros complejos, como presentaciones de venta (*pitch books*), memorandos para comités de inversión, análisis de consecuencias de fusiones y adquisiciones (M&A), revisiones de carteras y documentación para consejos de administración.

"Estamos implementando IA generativa para garantizar que todos los documentos de una transacción estén perfectamente verificados y conciliados al compartirlos con un cliente o un responsable de la toma de decisiones", afirmó Charlie Schilling, consejero delegado de Macabacus. "A medida que la IA se utiliza cada vez más para crear modelos y presentaciones, nosotros empleamos esa misma tecnología para minimizar los riesgos de contenido incoherente o alucinaciones en entregables de gran trascendencia, donde nuestros clientes no pueden permitirse cometer errores".

Deck Check AIR está integrado directamente en PowerPoint, por lo que los analistas y asociados no se ven obligados a utilizar una herramienta o aplicación independiente; además, es compatible con los modelos de Anthropic, OpenAI y Gemini, lo que permite a los clientes emplear sus propios LLM para la revisión de presentaciones. Esto les posibilita gestionar el consumo de tokens y, al mismo tiempo, mantener la seguridad de sus datos. Macabacus no utiliza datos de los clientes para entrenar sus modelos de IA, ni accede, almacena o conserva la propiedad intelectual de ningún cliente.
