title: As AI reshapes the workforce, boards face a governance challenge, says Deloitte Global Survey
excerpt: Key takeaways Only 16% of respondents say their organizations have an established strategy addressing technology transformation's impact on the...
lede: Global survey finds many organizations still treat human capital and technology transformation as separate governance matters
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from As represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Global survey finds many organizations still treat human capital and technology transformation as separate governance matters

As AI reshapes jobs, operating models and organizational culture, many companies are still developing the workforce strategies and governance practices needed to respond. The Deloitte Global Boardroom Program finds that only 16% of respondents say their organizations have an established strategy for addressing the workforce impact of technology transformation, even as AI adoption and investment accelerate.

The research, based on a survey of 806 board members and C-suite executives across 53 countries and in-depth interviews with 15 board chairs and directors, suggests that many organizations continue to treat technology transformation and human capital as separate governance matters. While 51% of respondents say they are incorporating human capital considerations into boardroom discussions around AI and other emerging technologies, nearly half (49%) say those discussions do not happen consistently.

"AI is not just transforming how work gets done. It is driving many organizations to reimagine their entire business models, with wide-ranging implications for skills, careers and workplace cultures," says Anna Marks, Deloitte Global Chair. "Pairing technology transformation with a talent pool that encompasses the right capabilities is what will help unlock real organizational value. The imperative is, therefore, for boards and management teams to work in a collaborative way to consider technology and talent strategies together, in a cohesive approach. This will help drive a value proposition that reaches far beyond productivity, where both businesses and people can thrive in the long term."

Board oversight currently centers on productivityProductivity is the workforce outcome boards discuss most frequently in connection with technology transformation, cited by 42% of respondents. Other considerations rank considerably lower, including attracting and retaining employees (15%), maintaining decision quality and human judgment (10%), employee well-being (9%), and employee trust (6%).

What's more, nearly half (49%) of those surveyed reported limited or no oversight of how technology-transformation investments are allocated between technology infrastructure and workforce enablement, while only 12% report full oversight with active monitoring and discussion.

body: U.S. housing is a $55 trillion market, making it one of the largest asset classes in the U.S. Yet despite its scale, broad-based investment exposure to U.S. home prices has remained difficult to access through traditional financial products. Index Industries was founded to close that gap.

Index Industries' first offering will be the U.S. Home Price Index (USHP Index), a proprietary benchmark for U.S. home prices. Calculated daily, it integrates data from the major housing indices into a single national measure, providing a continuous and comprehensive read on home prices. The index is intended to support housing-market research, reporting, and portfolio monitoring and housing-related financial products.

Index Industries is co-founded by Josh Rosenthal, who joins as CEO following his role as President and General Partner of Polychain Capital, and Brian Hardecker, a former Principal at Blackstone and the Founder and CEO of Longmark, a leading residential real estate platform formed in 2021 that has $2 billion in assets under management. Index Industries combines two worlds of expertise to bring breakthrough tokenization technology to new real estate assets.

"Indexing is one of the most important and least celebrated innovations in modern finance. It reduces the expertise and cost barriers to investing in an entire market, which is what U.S. housing needs," said Josh Rosenthal, co-founder & CEO of Index Industries. "I've spent my career looking for industry-shaping financial technology, and Index Industries is exactly that. It has the potential to change how the world sees housing: not just as a roof over your head or something that is out of reach, but as an investable asset class."

"U.S. housing is a massive market. It accounts for roughly a quarter of the aggregate value of the U.S. economy, yet it draws far less attention because there haven't been accessible ways to take a position in it," said Brian Hardecker, co-founder and chairman of Index Industries and CEO of Longmark Group. "Housing is uniquely inflation-protected, uncorrelated to other asset classes, and has arguably been one of the most stable paths to wealth accumulation. It hasn't seen the benefits of financial innovation that other sectors have. That's beginning to change with USHP, and we're proud to play a role."

"Real estate is one of tokenization's biggest opportunities, but bringing a $55 trillion asset class onchain requires traditional institutional infrastructure no crypto-native team has ever had. That's the gap Index Industries closes. It's rare to see two worlds of expertise converge at this caliber: traditional institutional rigor paired with scalable, secure, compliant technology that will unlock access and liquidity for the world's largest asset class. Index Industries' partnership with Longmark made leading this investment an easy decision for Lightspeed," said Justin Overdorff, Partner at Lightspeed Venture Partners.

As network and security architectures evolve at an unprecedented rate, manual test configuration and automation have become increasingly difficult to scale. As AI agents and agentic workflows become part of network and security operations, test infrastructure must be able to participate in those same AI-driven workflows.

The integration of VIAVI's award-winning MCP Server Framework simplifies the interaction between infrastructure testing tools and AI clients, and reduces reliance on GUIs, scripts or APIs. The MCP Server Framework includes an autonomous error correction loop to detect and self-correct test tool misconfigurations, with human review checkpoints maintaining oversight and safe operations at critical points in the testing process. expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Wire Issuer represents a significant milestone in verifiable sportsbook infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Under the agreement, ANTA Group will continue its humanitarian support from 2026 to 2029, providing UNHCR with US$1.5 million in cash and 1.2 million items of sportswear and equipment through the China Charity Federation and the Chinese Red Cross Foundation, with the approval of the relevant government ministries. The renewed partnership aims to reach another 300,000 young people in Ethiopia, Kenya, Burundi and elsewhere in Africa who have been forced from their homes and to improve their access to safety, learning and well-being through education and sport. Hence by 2029, the aim is to have reached a cumulative total of 600,000 young people over six years.

The agreement was signed by Wu Yonghua, Executive Director and Co-CEO of ANTA Group, and Tressa Rae Finerty, Deputy High Commissioner of UNHCR, in the presence of Ambassador Li Chijiang, Chargée d'Affaires a.i. of the Permanent Mission of China to the United Nations Office at Geneva and other International Organizations in Switzerland; Ding Shizhong, Board Chairman of ANTA Group; Olympic champion and ANTA brand ambassador Fan Zhendong; and members of ANTA Group's senior management team. Under the framework of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and in response to the challenges of people forced to flee, ANTA Group and UNHCR established a global partnership in 2023 and launched the Moving for Change international program of humanitarian assistance. By supporting UNHCR's two global initiatives, Primary Impact and Sport for Protection, the program provides funding and equipment to refugee camps in several African countries, including Ethiopia, Kenya and Burundi. The goal is to support forcibly displaced young people in accessing education and sport, giving them equal opportunities to experience the joy of sport, study and grow with confidence and dignity.

Ding Shizhong, Board Chairman of ANTA Group, said: "As a world-leading sportswear group, we look beyond the commercial value we create to the social value we can add. Anchored in our vision of 'becoming a respected, world-leading enterprise', we are committed to driving positive change for society and contributing to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. In China, the sports philanthropy programs we support have reached more than 10 million young people. Now we are extending that experience into international humanitarian assistance, so that what we leave around the world is not just our brands' footprint, but a Chinese company's journey of responsibility. We look forward to building on our new three-year partnership to help forcibly displaced young people rebuild their lives with confidence, integrate into their communities and move towards a brighter future through sport."

Tressa Rae Finerty, Deputy High Commissioner of UNHCR, said: "Young people forced to flee need more than safety. They need opportunities to learn, develop their talents and feel part of a community. By bringing together education and sport, our partnership with ANTA helps create those opportunities and supports young refugees to build their futures."

As a witness to the signing ceremony, Ambassador Li Chijiang, Chargée d'Affaires a.i. of the Permanent Mission of China to the UN Office at Geneva and Other International Organizations in Switzerland, said: " China firmly upholds true multilateralism and contributes to global refugee governance through concrete actions. Chinese companies are playing an increasingly important role, engaging more deeply in various areas such as humanitarian assistance, material transportation, professional knowledge sharing, and innovative solutions, contributing Chinese wisdom and strength to the international humanitarian cause."

Olympic table tennis champion and ANTA brand ambassador Fan Zhendong, who witnessed the signing in person, said: "What sport has given me is much more than my experiences in competition. It has given me confidence and courage in the face of difficulty, and the strength of striving side by side with others. I hope children who have been forced to leave their homes can have the chance to take part in sport, make friends and find joy through it. I greatly appreciate ANTA's meaningful work in philanthropy and charity. This is the kind of social value a sports brand should aspire to. I'm proud to attend this event, and I hope more people will pay attention to and support this humanitarian cause."

Organized by Tanya Meléndez-Escalante, MFIT's general manager and the 2026 recipient of the Vilcek Prize in Fashion and Culture, Fashioning Desire: Willy Chavarria and Bárbara Sánchez-Kane examines the ways in which two influential designers draw on their Mexican heritage, queer identities, and personal experiences to challenge and expand contemporary fashion. The Vilcek Prize in Fashion and Culture recognizes foreign-born individuals who have made extraordinary contributions to writing, curation, documentation, and image-making in the American fashion industry.

"An exhibition dedicated to their work represents a significant contribution to the growing scholarship on fashion, gender, and identity, shedding light on how these issues shape fashion within LGBTQ and Latinx communities," says Tanya Meléndez-Escalante, curator of the exhibition. The bilingual exhibition is organized thematically, bringing together works by both designers that reveal shared aesthetics and ideas. Chavarria is of Mexican and Irish descent, while Sánchez-Kane's mother is of Irish American descent and his father is Mexican.

These audiovisual pieces will be displayed as examples of the porosity of personal identity and the relationship between fashion and art. Ephemera and fashion accessories will be placed in vitrines, inviting viewers to examine them closely. This opening section will allow visitors to experience the vision of both designers and will provide an immersive introduction to their worlds.

A central theme of the exhibition is the crossing and porosity of borders—geographic, disciplinary, and even gender-related. body: In a warning issued during Fraud Awareness Week, Nomorobo cautions that the greatest danger of AI-enabled scams may not be fake voices or videos, but how easily scammers can gather and exploit personal information to establish credibility before a conversation even begins—making it harder for consumers to recognize who is really on the other end of the line.
Holiday Season is Ripe for Scams, AI is Making them Harder to Spot

"Artificial intelligence is giving scammers the ability to manufacture trust," said Matt Mizenko, Managing Director of Nomorobo. "They can make a message sound more natural, a conversation feel more personal and a voice sound remarkably familiar. Consumers need to understand that just because something sounds real doesn't mean it is real."

In 2025, Nomorobo blocked 107 million unwanted robocalls and text messages, including 86 million unwanted robocalls and nearly 21 million unwanted texts. Nomorobo estimated that 13 million of the blocked calls were malicious attempts to steal money. More than half of unwanted texts analyzed were scams, and 90% of those scam texts used scare tactics to pressure recipients into responding.
Scammers are also making calls look increasingly familiar. Seventy-four percent of robocalls analyzed by Nomorobo used area-code spoofing, making the incoming number appear to be local.

Recently, the Federal Trade Commission has warned that scammers are using AI-powered voice cloning to impersonate family members, friends, business executives and others to obtain money from consumers. AI can help scammers collect, organize and connect publicly available and potentially exposed personal information, including names, relationships, locations, employment details and other facts about an individual's life. Armed with those details, a scammer can open a conversation with information that sounds familiar and credible, making it much easier to convince someone they are speaking with a legitimate person or organization.

"De cryptomarkt werd meegesleurd door dezelfde 'risico-aversie'-krachten die ook verantwoordelijk waren voor de uitverkoop van AI-aandelen. In tegenstelling tot eind 2025 en begin 2026 zijn crypto-pullbacks relatief ondiep geweest. ETH is met dertien percent gedaald ten opzichte van de recente piek, terwijl Amerikaanse halfgeleiders ($SOXX) in dezelfde periode met twintig percent zijn gedaald. Wij geloven dat dit verder bewijs is dat er een crypto-bullmarkt gaande is," aldus Thomas "Tom" Lee, voorzitter van Bitmine.

"Bitmine heeft de afgelopen week aandelen teruggekocht en daarbij 2,04 miljoen aandelen verworven tegen een gemiddelde prijs van 22,48 dollar. Wanneer het management van mening is dat de aandelen van Bitmine relatief ondergewaardeerd zijn, is het bedrijf van plan aandelen terug te kopen op een manier die de winst per aandeel verhoogt, afhankelijk van de marktomstandigheden en binnen de bestaande machtiging tot terugkoop. Het optimaliseren van de aandeelhouderswaarde blijft ons belangrijkste doel," vervolgde Lee.

In 2026 heeft Bitmine 22,9 miljoen gewone aandelen teruggekocht, tegen een gemiddelde prijs van 17,48 dollar of een totaalbedrag van 399,6 miljoen dollar. "Dit is de grootste terugkoop van gewone aandelen ooit uitgevoerd door een crypto-treasurybedrijf en weerspiegelt onze toewijding aan de aandeelhouders," aldus Lee.

"Wij denken dat Bitmine goed gepositioneerd is om beter te presteren dan de cryptomarkt tijdens de hausse die we verwachten, aangezien de onderneming haar concurrentiepositie het afgelopen jaar heeft versterkt, midden in een cryptowinter (bearmarkt)", zei Lee.

"Over de afgelopen week hebben we 10.452 ETH verworven. De staat van dienst van Bitmine op het gebied van het consequent aankopen van crypto is ongeëvenaard door enige andere beursgenoteerde onderneming ter wereld. Bitmine heeft sinds de start van de ETH-treasurystrategie op 30 juni 2025 elke week ETH gekocht", aldus Lee.

body: Ces résultats mettent en lumière un message central : Les incidents internes se produisent rarement du jour au lendemain. Les facteurs psychologiques et comportementaux, allant des conflits au travail aux pressions financières, en passant par les crises personnelles, les influences extérieures et les erreurs humaines, peuvent modifier progressivement le comportement d'un individu et accroître sa vulnérabilité aux risques internes.

Le risque interne est fondamentalement un défi organisationnel centré sur les personnes. Les organisations, qu'il s'agisse d'entreprises privées, d'opérateurs d'infrastructures critiques ou d'institutions gouvernementales, évoluent désormais dans un environnement où des acteurs hostiles tels que les services de renseignement étrangers, les groupes criminels organisés et les concurrents commerciaux ciblent activement les employés au sein de ces organisations. Ces employés possèdent quelque chose que la technologie ne peut pas fournir : Connaissance du contexte, vision opérationnelle et accès légitime.

L'ampleur du défi est considérable, comme le confirme une récente publication du Service général de Renseignement et de Sécurité des Pays-Bas (AIVD). Selon d'autres sources citées dans le rapport Signpost Six, 83 % des organisations ont connu de tels incidents au cours des douze derniers mois, tandis que seulement 23 % affirment être suffisamment équipées pour les prévenir efficacement. Le coût moyen pour une organisation peut atteindre 17,5 millions d'euros par an, l'impact des incidents étant de plus en plus sensible dans les secteurs de la défense et des infrastructures critiques.

Le rapport montre que les organisations ne peuvent pas se fier uniquement à des mesures de cyber-sécurité pour faire face à un risque fondamentalement lié aux personnes. Avoir une vue d'ensemble complète des vulnérabilités existantes est un point de départ essentiel. Une approche efficace des menaces interne exige que les organisations reconnaissent et analysent les changements de comportement et les anomalies techniques.

De plus, les mesures de sécurité physique doivent être combinées à la surveillance des comportements inhabituels, au renforcement de la résilience des employés et à la capacité de réagir rapidement. Dans le contexte géopolitique actuel, il devient de plus en plus urgent pour les organisations européennes de renforcer rapidement leur sensibilisation et leur résilience face aux risques internes.
Rapport complet : La psychologie du risque interne

body: October brought weaker sales, more price cuts, and a downgrade in the national market ranking

October marked another step backward for the new home market. Sales declined 3.1% month-over-month and 11.7% year-over-year, a considerably steeper annual decline than September's 4.6% drop. The weakness was widespread, with pending sales declining year-over-year across all of Zonda's select markets. The national Zonda Market Ranking also slipped into slightly underperforming territory for the first time since January 2025.

The latest figures reinforce what builders have been telling us for months. Zonda's October builder sentiment survey found that 86% of builders reported slower-than-expected demand, up from 84% in September. In their comments, builders pointed to declining traffic, limited buyer urgency, and growing frustration with the effectiveness of incentives.

"One of the biggest challenges for builders right now is generating enough buyer interest in the first place," said Sarah Bonnarens, director of economic research for Zonda and NewHomeSource. "Builders still have an advantage when it comes to pricing and financing flexibility, but those tools can only do so much when buyer traffic is down. The challenge is keeping sales moving without putting even more pressure on margins."

Zonda's new home sales metric counts the number of new home contract sales each month and accounts for both cancellations and seasonality. This metric shows there were 638,568 new homes sold in October on a seasonally adjusted annualized rate. This was a decline of 3.1% from last month and a drop of 11.7% from a year ago. On a non-seasonally adjusted basis, 50,770 homes were sold, 11.6% lower than last year and 2.8% below the same month in 2019.

Incentives remain a key feature of the new home market, helping to sustain sales activity amid ongoing affordability pressures. In October, 64% of new home communities offered incentives on to-be-built homes and 83% on quick move-in supply. Note, these are only publicly available incentives so they will underrepresent overall usage.

Executive Produced by Anderson and produced by the three-time Emmy-nominated team behind Hallmark Channel's Home & Family, The Moll House™ transforms the traditional podcast experience through deeply personal conversations that move beyond press-tour talking points to reveal how "home has shaped who we are, how we love, what we have survived, and who we are becoming." Each episode is filmed inside one of Anderson's thoughtfully designed homes in Malibu, Dallas, Santa Fe, and Knoxville, where every room is intentionally created to encourage openness, reflection, and authentic conversation.

Rather than approaching this work as a psychologist or clinician, Anderson brings decades of experience as a researcher, communicator, interviewer, designer, bestselling author, and trusted lifestyle expert. The Psychology of Home™ translates this emerging research into accessible conversations about how the spaces we create, and the emotional lives we cultivate within them, influence stress, relationships, identity, resilience, healing, and our sense of belonging. A house may be made of walls, rooms and a roof, but a home is built from far more than its physical design. It is shaped by the words we speak, the emotional energy we create, the relationships we nurture, the rituals we repeat, the memories attached to our spaces, and whether the people inside feel safe, seen, connected, or alone.

The inaugural season features an extraordinary lineup of guests, including Brooke Burke, Roma Downey, Debbie Matenopoulos, Sarah Greenberg, Louise Hazel, David Kessler, Kelly Rizzo, Cameron Mathison, Dr. Shefali, Keltie Knight and Monique Lhuillier, with additional guests to be announced.

During that chapter of her life, creating a home was never about aesthetics. It was about creating safety, stability, hope, and an emotional foundation for herself and her family. Those experiences ultimately became the foundation of The Psychology of Home™, which serves as the cornerstone for her new podcast, The Moll House™.

title: Canada Is Posting More Cybersecurity Jobs, but Fewer Offer a First Step
excerpt: The Canadian Cybersecurity Network has released its Q3 2026 Workforce Intelligence Report, revealing a serious contradiction in Canada's...
lede: New CCN report finds entry level opportunities falling as skills convergence reshapes cybersecurity work
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Canada represents a significant milestone in verifiable regulation infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: New CCN report finds entry level opportunities falling as skills convergence reshapes cybersecurity work
Cybersecurity hiring reached 728 postings in the third quarter, rising 9.8 percent from Q2 and 64.7 percent from the same period in 2025.
Yet junior and entry level roles fell from 4.1 percent of postings in Q2 to just 1.5 percent in Q3. Approximately 27 opportunities became only 11 in one quarter.

"Canada cannot solve its cybersecurity talent shortage by asking every candidate to arrive experienced," said François Guay, Founder and CEO of the Canadian Cybersecurity Network. "We are increasing cybersecurity hiring while removing the first step into the profession. If businesses continue competing for experienced people without creating opportunities to develop new talent, the shortage will not be solved. It will be institutionalized."

Several factors may be contributing to the decline. Employers are combining cybersecurity, privacy, governance, cloud, data, artificial intelligence and business responsibilities into fewer positions. AI tools are absorbing some junior tasks, while lean security teams increasingly favour candidates who can contribute immediately.
This reflects a broader shift CCN describes as skills convergence.

The winning solution is built on FinBox DeviceConnect and Sentinel AI. Both now sit at the core of a new integrated risk platform on Sentinel AI, which FinBox launched at SFF 2026.

The presentation was judged by senior leaders from Citi, JPMorganChase, BNP Paribas Wealth Management, Finastra and 1982 Ventures.

Credit risk and fraud risk draw on many of the same customer signals, yet they are often assessed in separate systems. Each system sees only part of the applicant. Risks get missed in the gap between them, and that gap widens as customer behaviour shifts and fraud tactics change.

body: In the news release, Evoke Security Launches Defender CTF, the First Hands-On Lab for Investigating AI Agent Incidents, issued Nov. 17, 2026 by Evoke Security over PR Newswire, we are advised by a representative of the company that changes have been made throughout the press release. Built from rogue-agent behavior Evoke sees in live environments, the lab shows security practitioners what agent evidence exists and how to investigate agent-involved security incidents effectively.

"The next incident most security teams investigate will involve an AI agent," said Jason Rebholz, co-founder of Evoke Security. "Agents are already running commands, moving sensitive data, and taking action across endpoint, SaaS, and cloud systems on behalf of employees. Most security teams have never investigated one, and most don't know which systems hold the evidence they'd need. We want them to learn that now, in a lab, not in the middle of a breach."

Inside the lab, participants get the complete record of what an agent did, drawn from the same data Evoke collects in customer environments: the prompts and instructions the agent received, every tool and MCP server call and what was passed to it, commands executed in the runtime environment, files and records accessed, and actions taken in SaaS applications and cloud services, each tied back to the person and the agent responsible. Participants see where each piece of evidence originates, what it reveals, and how the pieces connect into a single timeline.

The CTF centers on the two most common issues Evoke observes in customer environments: employee misuse of agents and agents that go rogue. Every individual step can look legitimate in isolation. The CTF shows how those steps add up to a security incident, and what it takes to prove it.

Working the case, participants separate what the user asked for from what the agent actually did, pinpoint where the agent went beyond its instructions, flag the suspicious behavior, and reconstruct the incident timeline. They also see how much of the case disappears without agent telemetry. Many teams can already pull in agent activity, from AI providers' compliance and audit logs to endpoint, SIEM, and identity data. What they cannot do today with existing tools is tie those sources into a single view that shows what the agent did and where it crossed the line, leaving threats missed and investigations stalled.

"Community health workers are some of the most trusted people in the neighborhoods they serve. Pairing that human trust with smart technology enables us to direct outreach efforts where the need is greatest and connect with residents who have less access to preventative care," said Tom Hughes, executive director of IPHA. "We know that early detection opens the door to a greater range of treatment options for those at highest risk, and this initiative shows that data-driven tools, in the right hands, can save lives."

In March 2026, 11 community health workers from eight local health departments received comprehensive training on the program's central solution, HealthPrism, a predictive modeling solution developed by Deloitte to help identify community health risks. The use of HealthPrism was a key factor in IPHA securing grant funding for the initiative that enabled community health workers to build trusted relationships with local residents outside of the clinical setting. The training used real-world scenarios to prepare them to identify and address colorectal cancer risk factors, and identify the communities where rates continue to be higher than average.

"Artificial intelligence is developing rapidly, and IPHA's work with HealthPrism shows how agencies can harness these powerful advancements to improve the health of our communities," said Aldila Lobo, Deloitte's State, Local and Higher Education leader. "This is a leading example of how human insight, supported by AI, gives small teams the tools they need to have a major impact."

The HealthPrism solution leverages machine learning and curates data from more than 300 publicly available and commercial datasets, including Data USA. It is designed to resolve data gaps common in public sources, particularly where transient, rural, or historically overlooked populations are underrepresented, to accurately model and map communities at increased risk for chronic conditions. This insights-driven approach is supported by strict data controls, encryption and privacy compliance.

Over the next two years, IPHA and those it works with will deploy HealthPrism in the field, monitor the program's effectiveness, evaluate screening outcomes, and document success to further demonstrate the initiative's impact.

body: Boardwalk Real Estate Investment Trust ("Boardwalk", the "REIT" or the "Trust") announced today that it has received approval from the Toronto Stock Exchange (the "TSX") to renew its normal course issuer bid (the "NCIB") for an additional one year period.

The NCIB allows the REIT to purchase up to 3,613,885 trust units of the Trust (the "Units") (representing approximately 10% of the public float of 36,138,854 Units issued and outstanding as of November 10, 2026) over a period of twelve months commencing on November 24, 2026. As of November 10, 2026, there are 45,318,334 Units issued and outstanding. The NCIB will expire no later than November 23, 2027. Under the NCIB, Units may be repurchased in open market transactions on the TSX, and/or alternative Canadian trading systems, or by such other means as may be permitted by the TSX and applicable securities laws. In accordance with the rules of the TSX governing normal course issuer bids, the total number of Units the REIT is permitted to purchase is subject to a daily purchase limit of 26,221 Units, representing 25% of the average daily trading volume of Units on the TSX calculated for the six calendar months ending October 31, 2026, provided, however, that the REIT may make one block purchase per calendar week which exceeds the daily repurchase restriction. All Units purchased by the REIT pursuant to the NCIB will be cancelled.

Purchases of Units will be made by Boardwalk in accordance with the requirements of the TSX.  In connection with the NCIB, the REIT intends to enter into an automatic purchase plan with TD Securities Inc. to allow for purchases of its Units during periods when the REIT would ordinarily not be permitted to make purchases due to regulatory restriction or self-imposed blackout periods. Purchases will be made in accordance with the Trust's discretion and based upon the parameters prescribed by the TSX.

Pursuant to a previous notice of intention to conduct a NCIB, under which the Trust sought and received approval from the TSX to purchase up to 4,018,000 Units during the period from November 24, 2025 to November 23, 2026, the Trust purchased the maximum permitted amount at a weighted average price of $65.26 per Unit.

Management of the REIT believes that proceeds from non-core asset sales can currently be deployed toward the purchase and cancellation of the Units on an accretive basis. Boardwalk believes the Units continue to trade at a price that is below their underlying value. Boardwalk is committed to enhancing stakeholder value and continually evaluates its capital allocation opportunities.

body: Die Ergebnisse unterstreichen eine zentrale Botschaft: Vorfälle durch Insider entstehen selten über Nacht. Psychologische und verhaltensbezogene Faktoren – von Konflikten am Arbeitsplatz über finanziellen Druck und persönliche Krisen bis hin zu externen Einflüssen und menschlichem Vehlverhalten – können das Verhalten einer Person schrittweise verändern und die Anfälligkeit für Insiderrisiken erhöhen.

Insiderrisiken sind im Grunde genommen eine menschenbezogene organisatorische Herausforderung. Organisationen – ob private Unternehmen, Betreiber kritischer Infrastrukturen oder staatliche Institutionen – agieren heute in einem Umfeld, in dem feindlich gesinnte Akteure wie ausländische Nachrichtendienste, organisierte kriminelle Gruppen und kommerzielle Wettbewerber gezielt Mitarbeiter dieser Organisationen ins Visier nehmen. Diese Mitarbeiter verfügen über etwas, das Technologie nicht bieten kann: Kontextwissen, Einblicke in die Betriebsabläufe und legitimen Zugang.

Das Ausmaß der Herausforderung ist beträchtlich, wie eine aktuelle Veröffentlichung des niederländischen Allgemeinen Nachrichten- und Sicherheitsdienstes (AIVD) bestätigt. Anderen im „Signpost Six"-Bericht zitierten Quellen zufolge waren 83% der Organisationen in den vergangenen zwölf Monaten von solchen Vorfällen betroffen, während nur 23% angeben, ausreichend gerüstet zu sein, um diese wirksam zu verhindern. Die durchschnittlichen Kosten für eine Organisation können jährlich bis zu 17,5 Millionen Euro betragen, wobei die Auswirkungen solcher Vorfälle im Verteidigungssektor und im Bereich kritischer Infrastrukturen zunehmend heikel werden.

Der Bericht zeigt, dass sich Organisationen nicht ausschließlich auf technische Sicherheitsmaßnahmen verlassen können, um ein grundsätzlich menschenzentriertes Risiko zu bewältigen. Ein wirksamer Ansatz zur Bewältigung von Insiderrisiken erfordert, dass Organisationen sowohl Verhaltensänderungen als auch technische Anomalien erkennen und analysieren. Ein umfassender Überblick über bestehende Schwachstellen ist hierbei ein wesentlicher Ausgangspunkt.

Darüber hinaus müssen physische Sicherheitsmaßnahmen mit der Erkennung ungewöhnlichen Verhaltens, der Stärkung der Resilienz der Mitarbeiter und der Fähigkeit zur schnellen Reaktion kombiniert werden. In Anbetracht der aktuellen geopolitischen Lage wird es für europäische Unternehmen immer dringlicher, das Bewusstsein und die Resilienz in Bezug auf Insiderrisiken rasch zu stärken.
Vollständiger Bericht: The Psychology of Insider Risk

The agreement paves the way for CME Group, the world's leading derivatives exchange, to list cash-settled futures contracts, pending regulatory review, based on the CME FSPI NBA benchmarks.

CME FSPI are benchmarks designed to systematically measure the cumulative performance of teams and athletes in prominent sports leagues. The play-by-play indexes that move throughout the course of each game will provide hedging vehicles and new investment opportunities to a broad range of institutional and individual investors.

Leigh Taylforth, FutureSports Co-Founder, said: "We have built our relationship with the NBA over the last four years, and it is incredibly rewarding to see that partnership evolve into something concrete: a set of rules-based basketball indexes trading on CME Group. With a league that has the popularity and international reach of the NBA, building out real financial market infrastructure is a logical evolution."

Scott Kaufman-Ross, NBA Executive Vice President, Media Distribution and Partnerships, said: "We are excited to partner with FutureSports and CME Group to create a new way for fans to engage with the NBA, with appropriate safeguards built in from the outset."

The NBA, FutureSports and CME Group are committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, transparency and market confidence in both the indexes and futures. FutureSports' indexes are administered using transparent, rules-based methodologies derived from official on-court NBA statistics, helping ensure that index values are determined objectively and independently. NBA will have no involvement in the determination, calculation or governance of the indexes, which are the purview of FutureSports.

title: Secomea reporta la necesidad de un acceso remoto seguro a los sistemas de refrigeración

expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Secomea represents a significant milestone in verifiable regulation infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: - Secomea reporta que los ciberataques a supermercados europeos ponen de relieve la necesidad de un acceso remoto seguro a los sistemas de refrigeración

Una segunda oleada de presuntos ciberataques contra los sistemas de refrigeración de supermercados plantea interrogantes urgentes sobre cómo los minoristas protegen su tecnología operativa crítica, al tiempo que mantienen servicios remotos esenciales

Los incidentes más recientes, registrados en Suecia, Bélgica y Luxemburgo, ponen de relieve un desafío creciente para los minoristas: la tecnología operativa (OT) encargada de garantizar la seguridad alimentaria está cada vez más conectada a sistemas externos y proveedores de servicios, lo que genera posibles riesgos de seguridad cuando dicha conectividad no está protegida de manera adecuada.

A diferencia de los ciberataques tradicionales, centrados en el robo de datos o la interrupción de servicios informáticos, los ataques a la tecnología operativa pueden tener consecuencias físicas inmediatas. La vulneración de los sistemas de refrigeración puede derivar en el deterioro de los alimentos, la interrupción de las operaciones, pérdidas económicas considerables y posibles riesgos para la seguridad alimentaria.

«Estos incidentes ilustran por qué la ciberseguridad ya no consiste únicamente en proteger la información. Cuando los atacantes interfieren en la tecnología operativa, las consecuencias se vuelven físicas», afirmó Michael Ferdinandsen, consejero delegado de Secomea, una empresa danesa de ciberseguridad industrial especializada en acceso remoto seguro.

«Para los minoristas, la cuestión no es si necesitan conectividad remota; sin duda la necesitan. La cuestión es si tienen un control suficiente sobre quién puede acceder a sus equipos, a qué pueden acceder y qué se les permite hacer».

body: Conformément à la loi sur la Narodowy Bank Polski, le gouverneur de la NBP préside le Conseil de politique monétaire et, en particulier, a la compétence exclusive pour convoquer ses réunions.

Un membre du Conseil désigné à l'avance ne peut présider les travaux du Conseil de politique monétaire que pendant une brève absence temporaire de son président, ce qui ne se produit qu'occasionnellement au cours de la première journée de la réunion, durant laquelle aucune décision n'est prise et qui est notamment consacrée à la présentation d'analyses économiques.

Il est toutefois évident que cette faculté de suppléance n'habilite pas le membre du Conseil ainsi désigné à exercer l'ensemble des attributions que la loi et le règlement intérieur confèrent au président du Conseil.

Le règlement intérieur du Conseil dispose notamment que les résolutions du Conseil sont signées par le président et par tous les membres ayant participé au vote. Parallèlement, la loi sur la NBP énonce les exigences spécifiques relatives à la présence des membres du Conseil lors de l'adoption des résolutions.

Cela signifie qu'un membre du Conseil désigné à l'avance ne peut suppléer le président du Conseil qu'à titre ponctuel et uniquement pour l'accomplissement d'actes déterminés au cours de la réunion du Conseil.

Il convient par ailleurs de souligner que tous les organes collégiaux de la NBP (le Conseil de politique monétaire et le Conseil d'administration de la Narodowy Bank Polski) exigent la présence et la participation active du gouverneur de la NBP.

title: Datalink Networks Responds to Critical Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities Impacting Global Web Infrastructure
excerpt: Datalink Networks, a nationally recognized managed services, cybersecurity, cloud, and IT consulting provider, today addressed a series of...

body: Recent PHP, Node.js, and certificate security concerns underscore the need for continuous vulnerability management and rapid remediation.

On Oct. 21, two critical vulnerabilities affecting PHP, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and collectively known as "PHP2Shell," prompted an alert from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution and affect PHP installations serving web requests. CISA has urged organizations to identify affected systems and immediately apply available security updates, prioritizing internet-facing infrastructure.

The disclosure comes amid additional security concerns involving Node.js and the global certificate trust ecosystem. Node.js released security updates addressing several high-severity vulnerabilities, including issues involving TLS hostname validation. Additionally, eight intermediate certificates associated with certificate authority eMudhra were found to contain weak private keys, creating concerns around fraudulent certificate issuance and website impersonation.

Together, these events highlight a broader cybersecurity challenge: organizations depend on layers of software, applications, infrastructure, and third-party technologies that must be continuously identified, monitored, and secured.

"What makes these events significant isn't just their technical severity. It's how deeply these technologies are embedded in the systems businesses rely on every day," said Kodi Oshiro, SOC Manager at Datalink Networks. "Organizations cannot control when the next critical vulnerability is discovered, but they can control how prepared they are to identify their exposure, respond quickly, and reduce their risk."

Datalink Networks encourages organizations to take a measured but immediate approach by identifying internet-facing assets and affected technologies, applying available security updates, monitoring for suspicious activity, and validating that existing cybersecurity controls are operating effectively.

Designed specifically for cryptocurrency systems, CCSS complements broader information security standards by adding specialized requirements for the management and protection of cryptographic keys and wallets. body: New infrastructure- including EDGE Connect, which reduces the liquidation risks of margin calls on nights and weekends - enables money movement and controlled capital access for AI agents, execution platforms and clearing houses

The new infrastructure allows institutions to establish pre-authenticated accounts with clearly defined permissions and capital limits. Trading algorithms and AI agents can then execute approved activities within those parameters without gaining unrestricted access to an institution's underlying accounts.

Institutions can pre-determine how much capital to deploy, by whom and for what purpose, including setting daily transaction limits. For example, an institution could authorize an agent to allocate up to $100,000 per day, and prevent it from accessing or moving any additional funds. The capabilities will be available to all EDGE Pro users. EDGE Markets' execution routing partners - River Markets, Open Markets, ParlayX and Pikkit - will also integrate them through EDGE's APIs, so traders can execute on the partner platform of their choice while using EDGE Pro for banking and capital allocation.

"Markets are becoming increasingly automated and global, but the infrastructure for accessing and moving capital on prediction markets falls short of real-world demand," said Seni Thomas, Founder and CEO of EDGE Markets. "EDGE Markets is creating a secure, programmable layer between institutional capital and the platforms, counterparties and agents authorized to use it. That allows firms to automate at scale while maintaining clear control over how much capital can move and where it can go, including nights and weekends."

EDGE Markets has also scaled EDGE Connect - their private banking rails - to address the structural challenge for perpetual and other 24/7 markets: trading never stops, but traditional banking rails still do. When a margin call occurs overnight or during a weekend, traders are often unable to send a bank wire before the required deadline. That creates unnecessary liquidation risk for market participants and can force clearing houses to maintain substantial reserves to cover the gap until banking systems reopen.

With EDGE Connect, traders can pre-authorize an approved clearing house to pull additional margin automatically, up to a predetermined limit. This allows legitimate margin obligations to be met when they arise while preserving strict controls over the amount and recipient.

body: The published decision affirmed the district court on all issues raised in the cross-appeals and the jury found that Ford misappropriated technology and breached their confidential disclosure agreement with InterMotive, a California manufacturer whose products enable specialty vehicle manufacturers and upfitters to integrate equipment with electronic systems.

The case resulted from InterMotive sharing technology with Ford, as they pursued a commercial relationship. Ford later introduced a competing Upfitter Interface Module. A federal jury found that Ford misappropriated InterMotive's trade secrets, infringed its trademark and engaged in unfair competition.

"This case should matter to every small manufacturer that develops valuable technology and has to share it with a much larger company to pursue a commercial relationship," said Howard & Howard attorney Andrew "Jake" Grove, who tried the case with colleague and intellectual property attorney Joseph Barber. "Being smaller does not mean you are powerless. But you need to protect the technology, document the relationship and be prepared to enforce those rights when necessary."

The Sixth Circuit also rejected Ford's effort to limit InterMotive's recovery of profits from the competing product. The ruling reinforces the availability of disgorgement as remedy in trade secret cases and confirms that defendants cannot import more restrictive patent-damages principles into trade secret litigation.

"Large companies sometimes assume that a smaller supplier will not have the resources or resolve to challenge them," Barber said. "InterMotive did. Our job was to match that resolve with a litigation strategy capable of going the distance against one of the world's largest automotive companies."
The Howard & Howard trial team included Jake Grove, Joe Barber, Jerry McGlynn, Dane Lepola, Michael Fawaz and Kristina Black.

The MDL now includes more than 2,500 pending cases in federal court and an additional 3,300 in California state court. The cases allege that Meta, Snap, TikTok, and YouTube knowingly engineered their platforms to maximize engagement among minors, despite knowing that certain design features caused anxiety, depression, self-harm, and disrupted learning, and left school districts to bear the financial and human consequences. The next federal bellwether trial for school district claims is scheduled for February 2027.

School districts in the litigation seek recovery for documented institutional costs, including mental health counseling, monitoring software, and the broader administrative burden of addressing a youth mental health crisis that school communities say these platforms deliberately created.

body: The article explains that truck accidents on major Rochester highways, such as I-390 and I-490, require a more thorough legal evaluation than standard car crashes. One key difference is the number of potentially responsible parties involved. In a typical car crash, liability often extends only to the drivers. But in a commercial truck accident, the trucking company, vehicle owner, maintenance providers, or even manufacturers may be held liable. This multi-layered approach to truck crash liability is especially relevant in cases involving serious injury or property damage.

Federal and New York trucking regulations create a web of legal obligations that don't exist for regular drivers. Wright explains that violations of hours-of-service rules, inspection requirements, or maintenance standards become smoking guns in injury cases. "I've won cases where the driver wasn't technically at fault for the crash itself, but the company forced them to drive 14 hours straight in violation of federal law," he notes. "That's negligence, and it's actionable."

The evidence in truck cases is completely different. "Trucks have black boxes, electronic logging devices, maintenance records, dispatch logs, driver qualification files—it's a treasure trove," Wright says. "But here's the catch: trucking companies only have to preserve that evidence if you send a spoliation letter immediately. Wait too long, and it gets deleted or 'lost.' I've seen critical evidence disappear within 30 days of a crash."

Insurance is where things get brutal. Commercial trucks carry policies worth $1 million to $5 million or more—but that also means insurance companies fight harder. "These aren't the adjusters you deal with in a fender-bender," Wright warns. "These are specialized teams with investigators, accident reconstructionists, and lawyers on speed dial. They'll have someone at the crash scene before the tow truck arrives, gathering evidence to deny your claim."

Wright emphasizes that trucking companies can be held liable for systemic failures, not just driver error. "We look at hiring practices, training records, safety ratings, prior violations—everything," he explains. "If a company knowingly hired a driver with a suspended license or ignored repeated safety complaints, that's corporate negligence. And that's where the real compensation comes from."

The stakes are higher because the injuries are catastrophic. "A fully-loaded semi weighs 80,000 pounds," Wright notes. "When that hits a 3,000-pound car, we're talking about spinal injuries, traumatic brain injuries, amputations, fatalities. These aren't soft-tissue cases. The medical claims alone can run into millions, which is why you need an attorney who knows how to handle complex truck litigation."

A Distinctive Spirit Rooted in Atacama and Coquimbo

Produced in Chile's Atacama and Coquimbo regions, Chilean Pisco is a grape-based spirit shaped by the geography, climate and agricultural traditions of northern Chile. Its production takes place across five valleys: Copiapó, Huasco, Elqui, Limarí and Choapa, where abundant sunshine, distinctive soils and significant temperature variations contribute to the character of the grapes.

Unlike spirits made from neutral agricultural bases, Chilean Pisco is distilled from wine produced with authorized grape varieties, including Moscatel de Alejandría, Moscatel de Austria, Moscatel Rosada, Torontel and Pedro Jiménez. Their diversity, combined with different production and aging methods, gives the category a broad range of aromatic profiles and styles, from fresh and floral expressions to more structured and complex aged spirits.

Established in 1931, Chile's Denomination of Origin for Pisco protects its geographical identity and establishes production requirements, linking the spirit to its designated regions and traditions. This combination of origin, grape varieties and production expertise is central to differentiating Chilean Pisco in the international spirits market.

The category is also gaining international commercial momentum. Chilean Pisco exports reached US$3.9 million in 2025, a 27.6% increase over 2024, when exports totaled US$3 million, following 31.4% growth from 2023. During 2025, Chilean Pisco reached 40 destination markets and more than 110 international buyers.

title: Data Breach Class Action Settlements Reach Record Levels in 2025
excerpt: Federal courts approved a record 139 data breach class action settlements in 2025, marking a new milestone in the growth of data breach...
lede: Federal litigation reaches new levels as cybersecurity risks increase
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Data represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Federal litigation reaches new levels as cybersecurity risks increase

The report, Data Breach Class Action Settlements: 2010–2025 Review and Analysis, examines 426 federal class action settlements approved between 2010 and 2025. As cybersecurity incidents have increased—in 2025 alone, approximately 279 million personal records were exposed in U.S. data breaches—so has litigation exposure.

"Data breaches have evolved from isolated incidents into a persistent business risk across industries," said report coauthor Vildan Altuglu, senior vice president and cohead of the consumer fraud and product liability practice at Cornerstone Research. "The steady rise in settlement activity, combined with shorter resolution timelines, suggests that data breach litigation has become a more established and predictable area of class action practice. Future litigants now have empirical data to benchmark their exposure and navigate resolutions."

High-Value Settlements—those reaching $50 million—have been relatively rare but have driven a disproportionate share of total settlement dollars. Since 2016, when the first such settlement was approved, there have been just 11 High-Value Settlements. But those settlements accounted for 61% of the $3.24 billion in total settlement dollars awarded over the last 15 years, despite representing only 3% of all monetary settlements.
Most settlements remain considerably smaller. The study found that 76% of monetary settlements resolved for $5 million or less, while only 6% exceeded $25 million.

The report also highlights differences across industries. Healthcare registered the highest volume of settlements, with 118 cases, while Financial Services generated the largest aggregate settlement value, at $1.2 billion, driven mainly by three High-Value Settlements totaling $904 million. Among major sectors, Entertainment recorded the highest median settlement value at $3.3 million per case.

title: Xryma Plc Wins Berlin Court Order Stopping Schirp Law Firm from Publishing False "Juicy Fields" Statements

expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Xryma represents a significant milestone in verifiable payments infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: Regional Court Berlin II grants injunction against the majority of challenged statements; finds Schirp failed to give Xryma Plc an opportunity to respond before publicly accusing it of investment fraud and money laundering

The challenged statements covered by the injunction include assertions published by Schirp on its own websites and via third-party platforms including EQS News, Ad-hoc-News and TradingView, claiming there were "very good reasons" or "sufficient grounds for suspicion" to hold Xryma responsible for investment fraud or money laundering, describing among others Xryma as "one party involved in the crime… still active in the market," and stating that Schirp had sent letters of demand accusing Xryma of money laundering. The Court found that these statements infringe Xryma's rights and ordered Schirp to stop making or repeating them. The false assertion of "money-laundering allegations" by Schirp is covered by the injunction.

The Court's reasoning was that Schirp went beyond permissible "suspicion-based reporting" by not giving Xryma an opportunity to respond before publicly accusing it, adding that a law firm addressing the public is bound by the same German press-law principles as press media, and is separately subject to a duty of objectivity under Section 43b of the German Federal Lawyers' Act on the Professional Code of Conduct for Lawyers (BRAO).

The Court noted, in particular, that no criminal investigation has been opened against any Xryma officer or employee, and that Schirp's publications were aimed at winning clients rather than informing the public. Xryma confirms that no criminal investigation has been opened against the Company, any of its officers or employees in relation to this or any other matter.

"We welcome the Court's ruling. It confirms what we have said from the outset: Xryma Plc, formerly ISX Financial EU Plc, was publicly accused of serious crimes, in explicit terms, without Schirp asking for our position or informing the public that we dispute the allegations. The Court found that Schirp fell short of what German law requires, including those expected of a law firm that was intent on building a client base around these claims. Separately, Schirp also claims to be running "multi million euro civil claims" against Xryma Plc, which to date, total less than €240,000 across 6 claimants, each of which claim Xryma is vigorously defending. Law firms should conduct themselves to a higher standard when making public claims.", stated Nikogiannis Karantzis, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Xryma Plc.

"Xryma has always taken its regulatory obligations very seriously. No investigation has been opened into Xryma or any of its officers or employees. We continue to cooperate with the authorities examining the Juicy Fields matter, including providing data and witness statements to law enforcement agencies."

Giancristofaro started posting videos on TikTok after seeing that the public often struggles to understand the legalities involved in criminal cases. After the murder of four college students at the University of Idaho in 2022, she began making videos to help people gain a better understanding of the criminal defense process and laws regarding the case. People appreciated the videos because Giancristofaro helped clarify confusing information about the case they were seeing dominate the headlines.  This led her to continue with other cases so people could better understand the issues in terms they could easily grasp.

According to the Pew Research Center, 37% of adults in the U.S. report that they use TikTok, and that number continues to grow each year. They report that around 55% of adults who use the popular app regularly get their news from it, while 95% say they use it for entertainment purposes. Giancristofaro's videos get millions of views, showing how much interest people have in that type of content.

On September 20, 2026, TikTok celebrates its 10th anniversary. Originally launched as Douyin from a small apartment in China in 2016, it expanded internationally a year later. The popularity of the app was greatly boosted in 2018, when it merged with the app Musical.ly, which featured people lip-syncing to songs. TikTok has surged in popularity as people find that the algorithm excels in serving up content that is unique to each person's interest. It has become an outlet for influencers of all types to find their unique audience, including for those who are interested in crime news, criminal defense, and related issues.

The Military Family Advisory Network's latest national survey found that one in five military and veteran families experience food insecurity, while a 2023 RAND study reported that approximately 25.8% of active-duty service members met the USDA definition of food insecurity. Research points to factors unique to military life, including frequent relocations, spouse unemployment, childcare expenses, housing costs, and unexpected moving expenses, as contributors to the problem.

"Military families make sacrifices every day in service to our country, yet too many continue to face challenges putting food on the table," said Dr. Anthony Hassan, president and CEO of Cohen Veterans Network. "Through CVN Gives Back and the generous support of RTX, we're able to expand assistance to local food banks serving military communities across the country. Together, we're helping ensure that military families have greater access to food and other essential resources."

CVN Gives Back is a natural extension of the network's commitment to addressing the challenges that affect the overall well-being of military families. In addition to providing mental health care, the network's 24 Cohen Clinics offer comprehensive case management services that help clients navigate food insecurity, employment, housing, education, and other social drivers of health.

"Strong support systems are essential for military families as they navigate the demands of service and civilian life," said Kristy Becerra, senior director of corporate social responsibility at RTX. "By partnering with Cohen Veterans Network and local food banks, we're helping ensure military families can access critical resources close to home while investing in the community partnerships that make lasting support possible."

Since its inception in 2016, CVN has treated over 110,000 clients and provided over 990,000 clinical sessions. The network treats a wide variety of mental health concerns, including depression, anxiety, military transition challenges, anger, PTSD, grief and loss, family issues, relationship problems, and children's behavioral problems. Therapy options include individual, couples, family, and group sessions. Care is available in-person and via CVN Telehealth, face-to-face video therapy.

ABOUT COHEN VETERANS NETWORK Cohen Veterans Network (CVN) is a 501(c)(3) national not-for-profit philanthropic organization for post-9/11 veterans, active-duty service members and their families. CVN focuses on improving mental health outcomes, operating a network of outpatient mental health clinics in high-need communities, in which trained clinicians deliver holistic evidence-based care to treat mental health conditions. It was established in 2016 by philanthropist Steven A. Cohen with a commitment of $275 million to build the network. Learn more about CVN at cohenveteransnetwork.org.

body: The complaint alleges that on March 24, 2021, the teacher screamed at, belittled, and manhandled the preschooler—pushing her to the ground, yanking her by the arm, dragging her across the classroom, and locking her alone in a dark closet. In addition, the lawsuit states the teacher threatened to call the police on the preschooler and told her that her parents wanted her to go to jail. Every incident was captured on the school's surveillance cameras.

Text messages cited in the lawsuit reveal Trinity Lutheran School's director and principal received more than four months of explicit warnings from a preschool teacher that she was approaching a mental health breakdown, including one in which she called a "meltdown at work" her "worst nightmare." The school's response, per the complaint, was to continue having come into work and sending her back to her classroom—prioritizing staffing over child safety.

The newly amended petition's most shocking allegations detail the inaction of Trinity Lutheran School administrators. The leaders failed to intervene at every step, even after the director watched recorded footage of the abuse the day it happened, the lawsuit claims, but never dropped in to the preschool classroom and made no attempts to remove the teacher. The suit also states staff repeatedly passed the preschool classroom's door while the 4-year-old was loudly crying and the teacher was screaming at her—they, too, failed to intervene.

The next morning, when the Killingsworths raised concerns, leaders at Trinity Lutheran School said nothing about what they observed on the footage—a silence the petition says lasted five days, despite Texas childcare laws requiring schools to immediately report these kinds of incidents and the principal's own testimony that parents have an "absolute right to know." Trinity Lutheran School leaders also failed to preserve material evidence, with hours of surveillance footage missing from the preschool classroom the day of the terrorizing incident, per the complaint.

"Trinity Lutheran School's leadership ignored state childcare laws and failed to stop a 4-year-old girl and her preschool classmates from being terrorized by a teacher while under the school's watch," says daycare injury attorney Russell Button of The Button Law Firm. "This is what happens when a school prioritizes its staffing schedule over a child's safety, then tries to bury the truth instead of owning up to their multiple failures that broke the law."

The case is Patrick and Mellissa Killingsworth, Individually and as parents and next friends of P.K., a minor child, vs. Evangelical Lutheran Trinity Congregation, Cause No. D230014C in the District Court of Tom Green County, Texas. A copy of the complaint can be accessed here.

Stablecoins have become a core settlement rail for institutions. Tokenized real-world assets, including money market funds and private credit, are moving from pilot to production as banks and asset managers bring traditional instruments onchain. Regulation is catching up: the United States now has federal stablecoin law and is negotiating market structure legislation, the European Union is implementing MiCA, and supervisors across Asia and the Middle East are setting their own standards. For the hundreds of banks, payment companies, and asset managers that operate on Fireblocks, those rules decide how fast they can build and grow onchain-based revenues.

As an SEC Commissioner and Acting Chairman, Roisman voted on more than one hundred rulemakings and over one thousand enforcement actions, and represented the agency before Congress and international bodies including the International Organization of Securities Commissions and the Financial Stability Board. He previously served as Chief Counsel to the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, and as Chief Counsel at NYSE Euronext. Most recently, at Cravath, he advised financial institutions and fintechs on digital asset regulation and testified before Congress on market structure legislation.

Michael Shaulov, Co-Founder and CEO of Fireblocks, said: "Having people who understand the mindset and missions of regulators enables us to help inform policymakers and support our clients as rules come into place. That matters now more than ever, as stablecoins scale into everyday payments and real-world assets move onchain at institutional pace. Elad has both been a regulator and a legal advisor to many of the world's most prominent financial institutions. As our customers move deeper into regulated finance, that experience will enable our infrastructure to adapt and lead in a dynamic regulatory environment."

Elad Roisman, Chief Regulatory and Policy Officer at Fireblocks, said: "Today, we stand at an exciting time where there has never been more interest and work done by regulators and legislators to enable further innovation in this important space. The work now is engaging with these policymakers on the rapidly evolving digital asset environment and supporting institutions as they build and grow the next phase of the financial system under the new regulations and laws. Blockchain revenues fell 28% in 2026 but rose again in Q3. Full-year 2026 blockchain revenues are expected to reach about $100 billion, down 28% from roughly $140 billion in 2025 and in line with the decline in digital asset prices - although relative to total digital asset market capitalization, revenues were flat. Onchain user-paid fees were $3.9 billion in Q3 2026 and estimated $14B for all of 2026.

Beneath the drawdown, the mix is changing. Revenues from institutional adoption, meaning revenue earned by institutions as owners (ETF, card network and chain fees) and from institutional clients, were 12% of blockchain revenues in 2026 through Q3, up from 6% in 2021. In dollars, they doubled over three years to $6.1 billion in the first half of 2026, though they fell $0.7 billion year over year as price-sensitive asset management, custody and staking fees declined; their share rose because total revenues fell faster. The report cuts the same total three ways: by who earns it (public companies, 16% in 2026), by what drives it (institutional and broader-economy adoption, 33% in Q3 2026 and 30% for the year) and by sector (blockchain infrastructure, 21% in Q3 2026).

Broader-economy adoption overtakes blockchain infrastructure. Revenues from broader-economy adoption, including tokenized assets, payments and prediction markets, grew 58% year over year in the first half of 2026, led by prediction markets and trading in tokenized real-world assets, and overtook blockchain infrastructure revenues in Q3 2026 for the first time (22% versus 21%). Institutional and broader-economy revenues together reached 33% of blockchain revenues in Q3 2026.

Public companies now earn 16% of blockchain revenues, up from 7% in 2022; the six largest account for about 60% of public-company blockchain revenue. Large banks and traditional finance incumbents that had negligible blockchain revenue three years ago are on track to earn $1B this year. One way this group expands its revenue is via acquisitions - and there have been quite a few lately: BVNK (Mastercard), OpenZeppelin (S&P Global), bitbank (SBI), Zodia Custody (Standard Chartered).

Dividend-paying tokens beat Bitcoin. 1kx's dividend-token index, which tracks protocols that distribute value to token holders, returned 82% through September 30, 2026, versus a 5% decline for Bitcoin; outperforming Bitcoin was rare in recent years. The index figures are hypothetical and based on backtests. A record 283 protocols distributed value to token holders in Q3 2026.

The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, charges CUI with violating Title IX by depriving women of equal opportunities to participate in intercollegiate athletics. The data offers a reliable view on the dynamic role that noncash interest plays in private credit markets, including the variance in PIK activity across EBITDA segments, geographies and sectors. For example, the Benchmarks indicate that on a global basis PIK use is currently moderating rather than accelerating. Across loans originated globally during the previous 12 months, PIK represented 2.86% of interest income as of October 10, 2026, compared with 6.67% across the global cohort of outstanding loans at the end of Q2 2026.

Dolan, President of Financial Advisory at Kroll says, "Private credit and private capital markets have demonstrated relatively solid fundamentals, despite a prolonged period of higher borrowing costs and economic uncertainty. PIK is an important part of understanding what is happening beneath headline returns in private credit; the distinction between interest paid in cash and interest added to debt matters when assessing liquidity, leverage, credit quality and ultimately value."

"Operating at the intersection of value, risk and transactions gives Kroll a unique perspective on these dynamics. As private markets continue to grow and become increasingly complex, independent data, analysis and expertise become more important in distinguishing isolated pressure from broader market trends, bringing greater clarity and peace of mind to investors."

"The growth and evolution of private credit have created a more diverse market, making it increasingly valuable to understand how financing structures are changing alongside it," says Marcel Schindler, Partner and Head of Private Debt at StepStone Group. This is according to the Redfin Home Price Index (RHPI), which uses the repeat-sales pricing method to calculate seasonally adjusted changes in single-family home prices. The RHPI measures how sale prices of homes have changed since their previous sale. October data covers the three months ending October 31, 2026.

Home prices continued to rise in October, but at a slower pace. Buyers gained more negotiating power than at any point in Redfin's records, which date back to 2013. Only three of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas tracked by us were seller's markets in October.

However, a buyer's market doesn't necessarily signal strong buyer's demand. "Mortgage rates are not that volatile right now, but they're still higher than they used to be. That's holding back demand and putting some downward pressure on prices, which have started to fall in many parts of the country," said Chen Zhao, Redfin's head of economics. "On a national level, we don't think prices will fall very much."

There's also more supply available now, but sellers are not willing to cut prices deeply. "Many sellers are still anchored to the prices they've seen over the past few years, and because few sellers are under pressure to sell, that puts a floor under prices," said Zhao.
Home prices rose in 30 of the 50 major U.S. metros month over month in October.

title: Distinctive BAT: Study reveals the most distinctive and iconic slogans of all time in the U.S.
excerpt: To settle the often-debated question of which slogan is the most distinctive and iconic of all time, Distinctive BAT, a leading brand research...
lede: A new research study of U.S. consumers, testing over 1,000 slogans, shows which are the most distinctive, with State Farm's tagline crowned the winner.
expertAnalysis: CryptoCasinoMedia Newsroom editorial evaluation: The official release from Distinctive represents a significant milestone in verifiable crypto casinos infrastructure and institutional industry convergence.
body: A new research study of U.S. consumers, testing over 1,000 slogans, shows which are the most distinctive, with State Farm's tagline crowned the winner.

Distinctive BAT tested more than 1,000 slogans among a nationally representative sample of 3,000 U.S. consumers. Respondents were shown each slogan with the brand name removed and asked whether they recognized it and which brand it belonged to. The slogans were ranked by their level of distinctiveness, i.e., how uniquely a recognized slogan is associated with the correct brand. It was measured using Distinctive BAT's proprietary BAT (Brand Asset Testing) score. The score combines three metrics: Asset Recognition (familiarity) plus Brand Attribution (correct brand linkage) minus Misattribution (incorrect brand linkage), with a top score of 200.

State Farm's "Like a Good Neighbor, ____________ Is There" was the highest-scoring slogan, with 181 out of a possible 200 points. Cathal Gillen, co-founder of Distinctive BAT, explained why: "State Farm has followed a lot of best practices when it comes to embedding a slogan. It has generally been quite consistent with its use. While the line has been retired for short stints over the years, whenever it's been in use, State Farm has put it front and center in its advertising. But the ultimate cultural stamp of approval is when a slogan escapes advertising and enters the wider conversation. There are countless parodies of 'Like a Good Neighbor' across social media, but the cherry on top was when Saturday Night Live turned the line into a hilarious sketch with Michael B. Jordan."

Gillen also highlighted the power of jingles: "State Farm's slogan, like many other high-performing ones, is just as well-known as a jingle as it is as a tagline, and the earworm nature of jingles helps embed them as taglines too." Other top-scoring taglines that also live on as jingles include "Two Scoops of Raisins" (No. 6) from Kellogg's Raisin Bran, "The Best Part of Wakin' Up" (No. 11) from Folgers and, of course, "I am stuck on __________ brand 'cause __________ stuck on me!" (No. 12) from Band-Aid. Both the State Farm and Band-Aid jingles were written by none other than Barry Manilow.

KFC came in second with its iconic "Finger Lickin' Good." Like State Farm, KFC uses its slogan in creative ways. Gillen explained, "The hardest-working taglines serve as a jumping-off point for a wealth of creativity. This is something we have seen time and time again in our client research, and it's evident here, with several high-scoring taglines playing a bigger role for their brands. KFC is the perfect example. The brand has leaned into 'Finger Lickin' Good' in lots of ways over the years."

Gillen added, "Nike's 'Just Do It' (No. 7) is another great example. It's been the central thought behind some of Nike's most successful advertising campaigns. Too often, taglines are used only as a sign-off at the end of a 30-second ad. It's naive to think that alone will be enough to stick in consumers' memories."

The motion follows an extraordinary sequence in which payment was tendered repeatedly to lenders associated with investor Tony Robbins, an independent director was purportedly removed, the lenders unsuccessfully sought emergency relief in West Virginia state court, and the power plant was placed into bankruptcy two days later.

The solution brings together unpaid walkouts, unresolved self-checkout theft, aisle concealment and cashier fraud. It organizes scattered incidents into prioritized cases with supporting video, helping teams focus their resources on high-value theft and recurring loss.

Trigo's analysis of repeat theft at self-checkout found typical return intervals of 2–7 days, similar to the shopping frequency of regular customers. Among the clearest repeat-offender cases, theft occurred on almost every visit. Viewed separately, those incidents can conceal a persistent pattern.

The financial impact can be disproportionate. In retail activity analyzed by Trigo, 2.5% of shoppers accounted for 60% of recorded loss—highlighting the value of finding and connecting the incidents behind sustained theft.

Trigo reports a 15× uplift in repeat-offender identification, measured across retailer deployments. The company also reports 50–70% faster investigation and evidence collection, helping teams spend less time searching footage and more time progressing cases.

"A repeat offender does not have to be a known offender," said Daniel Gabay, co-founder and CEO of Trigo. "A walkout in one store and theft at self-checkout in another can look like unrelated events. Following the products gives us the context to connect them. The Theft Analysis Engine helps retailers uncover those patterns and build stronger cases around the theft causing the greatest harm."
