body: Employees now hand AI agents real work: reading files, calling tools, and handling sensitive data on their behalf. As that work moves to the cloud, it moves away from the endpoint, where security teams have spent a decade building visibility. An agent can complete a legitimate task and take an unexpected action along the way. Without the full record of what the agent did, security teams can't tell routine agent work from the opening move of an incident.

"Agents are part of today's workforce, and they're being misused and going rogue every day," said Jason Rebholz, Co-Founder and CEO of Evoke Security. "The challenge isn't knowing an agent ran. It's understanding what that agent did and what new risks it created. In incident response, the first question is always 'what happened?' If an agent did its work somewhere you can't see, you can't answer that question. Extending our Claude Cowork coverage deeper into the virtual environment closes that gap."

Existing security tooling wasn't built for how agents operate. Without agent-specific detection and response capabilities, security teams can struggle to distinguish normal agent operations from risky behavior. Evoke's platform monitors the full agent trajectory with a detection-in-depth approach, identifying risky behavior and steering the agent to a safer path or blocking unauthorized actions.

The integration builds on Evoke's mission to secure the agentic workforce: discovering the agents running across the organization, understanding their exposure, and detecting and responding to the agent activity that matters. Evoke's recent Rogue Agent Assessment shows how these risks surface in real environments today.
The integration with Claude Cowork is planned for a future release. Organizations interested in learning more about Evoke's AI agent detection and response capabilities can visit evokesecurity.com.

body: Berman & Simmons attorneys Travis Brennan and Chuck Hehmeyer secured the largest non-death medical malpractice verdict in Maine history for a man left permanently paralyzed due to medical negligence.

After nearly two weeks of trial, testimony by thirteen expert witnesses, and approximately three hours of deliberation, on June 18, 2026, the jury found Northern Light AR Gould Hospital and Northern Light Health negligent for plaintiff Robert Giordano's permanent paralysis. The record damages will cover his extraordinary past and future medical expenses, pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, emotional distress,  permanent impairment, and loss of consortium.

"The jury's verdict provided validation for our client that this tragic situation never should have happened," Attorney Brennan told the Bangor Daily News in an interview about the record-setting case result. "Northern Light first missed a dangerous finding on Robert's imaging study and failed to follow its own internal policies on reporting this critical finding. Next, Northern Light providers dismissed Robert when he sought help for new and alarming symptoms. This verdict will allow Robert to secure the vital medical equipment, supplies, and services that he requires to deal with the devastating and permanent injuries he suffered."

The case arose from the negligent medical care of Mr. Giordano, a 40-year-old Madawaska man who presented to the emergency room at Northern Light A.R. Gould Hospital in Presque Isle in December 2020 after a fall. Although a CT scan was performed, the radiologist failed to identify a large, bony calcification that had invaded Giordano's spinal canal and raised concern for spinal cord compression. Giordano was discharged with no knowledge that he had a ticking time bomb in his spine.

Over the following six weeks, Giordano's neurological symptoms progressively worsened. When he returned to his primary care provider the day before he was paralyzed and reported that he could no longer stand without falling, the provider dismissed his symptoms as an attempt to obtain pain medication and diagnosed him with chronic pain. An orthopedic specialist who saw Giordano that same day failed to recognize his symptoms were concerning for a neurologic emergency and failed to instruct Giordano to immediately go to the emergency department for evaluation.

"As the patient developed progressive neurologic deficits over the next six weeks, people were unaware that he had this ticking time bomb in his spine. It then detonated on Jan. 30, with him becoming fully and permanently paralyzed," Attorney Brennan explained.

body: BLUETTI, a global provider of portable power and energy storage solutions, offers a range of portable power stations designed to meet different energy needs, from household emergency backup to outdoor adventures, road trips and off-grid living.

Power outages can disrupt daily routines, affecting lighting, internet connectivity, communication devices and essential household appliances. Portable power stations provide an alternative source of electricity during temporary grid disruptions, helping households maintain access to essential devices. Unlike conventional fuel-powered generators, they operate quietly without producing direct exhaust emissions during use.
Energy for RV Travel, Camping and Outdoor Adventures

Beyond household backup, portable power stations offer greater flexibility for RV owners, campers and outdoor enthusiasts. Whether travelling in a motorhome, spending a weekend camping or exploring remote destinations, users can power electronics and selected appliances without relying entirely on conventional electrical connections.

Compatible solar panels provide another charging option, allowing users to replenish their power stations using sunlight in suitable outdoor conditions. Vehicle charging solutions also offer additional flexibility, making it easier to maintain power while travelling. Together, these options support a more independent and convenient outdoor lifestyle.

Selecting a portable power station involves considering battery capacity (Wh), output power (W), portability and charging flexibility. Compact models are suitable for everyday electronics and short outdoor trips, while higher-capacity systems can support more demanding household backup and off-grid applications.

Verified outcomes are recorded and fed back into subsequent AI reasoning as historical performance context, supporting ongoing evaluation of forecasting behaviour across domains and market conditions.
